state_program_name: Personal Care Home (PCH, 2–24 beds, Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-62) and Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds, ch. 111-8-63), permitted by DCH Healthcare Facility Regulation Division; Medicaid via the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP / SOURCE Alternative Living Services)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Georgia residential care program. It covers:

- a **Personal Care Home (PCH)** of 2–24 beds, governed by Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-62, or
- an **Assisted Living Community (ALC)** of 25 or more beds, governed by Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-63.

The manual is also written for communities that serve Medicaid residents through the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP and SOURCE Alternative Living Services).

The manual has four jobs:

1. **Direct staff and residents.** Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07 (ALC) and 111-8-62-.07 (PCH), the governing body must implement written policies, procedures and practices that support dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy in a safe environment. These policies must give direction to staff and residents on the minimum topics the rule lists.
2. **Show compliance.** Georgia DCH has no separate policy-review form. The applicant signs a notarized Affidavit of Compliance saying the mandated policies and procedures have been developed and will be implemented immediately on licensure. DCH inspects without notice, and the policies must be readily available for review during an inspection.
3. **Keep practice consistent.** Admissions, care planning, medications, emergencies, reporting, discharge and records should be handled the same way by every shift and every staff member.
4. **Protect residents.** Residents' rights, safety, freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation, and access to the Long-Term Care Ombudsman are built into every policy.

This manual does not replace the rules. If anything in it conflicts with a current Georgia statute or rule, the statute or rule controls and the manual must be corrected.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**Before you start: customize it.** This is a template. Every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every bracketed field (administrator or on-site manager, governing body members, licensed capacity, permit number, memory care status, Medicaid waiver participation, local contacts) must be completed for your community. Delete the sections for the license type you do not hold. Use the ALC (25+ beds) content for ch. 111-8-63 and the PCH (2–24 beds) content for ch. 111-8-62. The two rule lists differ in order and wording.

**Adopt it.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the adoption in its minutes, with the date and the signatures of the responsible officers. The governing body is also accountable for overseeing compliance with it.

**Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually. Review it again whenever:
- a rule is amended (for example, ch. 111-8-63-.09 was amended effective May 21, 2025),
- DCH issues a new checklist or form,
- licensure, ownership, capacity or services change (including adding or dropping memory care),
- an inspection report, plan of correction or incident shows a gap.

Record each revision with its date, the reason and who approved it.

**Train staff.** Every staff member must be trained on the policies that apply to their role and must acknowledge it in writing. Training records must be kept. Retrain whenever a policy changes. Rules .09 (ALC) and 111-8-62-.09 (PCH) set separate training requirements for staff; see those rules for current hour and timing requirements.

**Keep it available.** Keep a complete, current copy where staff can reach it at all times. It must be readily available to DCH inspectors on request, including during unannounced inspections.

**Find things fast.** The manual is organized item by item so each lettered paragraph of the official rule can be located quickly during a survey.

**Use Appendix A.** Appendix A maps every official item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to confirm that nothing is missing, and to answer an inspector's question about where a requirement is addressed.

**Verify before you rely on it.** Some rule paragraphs were only partly retrieved in preparing this manual (for example, the complete lists in .07 and the remaining paragraphs of .13, .15, .16, .21, .25 and .29). Read the full current text of each rule before finalizing the manual. Items marked as unverified in the regulatory framework section must be confirmed with DCH.

## Regulatory Framework

### Governing rules

The rules below were used in preparing this manual. They are cited by their exact cite text.

**Licensing chapters and authority**
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63**: Rules and Regulations for Assisted Living Communities (rules .01–.34).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62**: Personal Care Homes. A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license.
- **O.C.G.A. §§ 31-2-7 and Chapter 7 of Title 31**: statutory authority for the ALC rules. The rule notes also cite O.C.G.A. 31-2-8, 31-2-9, 31-7-1 et seq. and 43-26-12.
- **O.C.G.A. § 31-7-12.4**: memory care centers; certificate required; staffing and training requirements.

**ALC rules (ch. 111-8-63)**

- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.05 (Application for Permit)

**PCH rules (ch. 111-8-62)**
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.03 (Definitions)
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.05 (Application for Permit)
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.06 (Permits)
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07 (Governing Body)
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.08 (Administrator Qualifications)
- Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.09 (Workforce Qualifications and Training)
- Rule 111-8-62 (staffing and change of ownership provisions)

**Related DCH rule chapters** referenced in the rules above: Ch. 111-8-25 (fees and sanctions), Ch. 111-8-100, Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans) and Ch. 111-8-12 (criminal background checks).

**Fees, program and administrator documents**
- DCH Schedule of Licensure Activity Fees
- DCH ALC Application Checklist
- CMS waiver 0112.R08.00 (Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver, expires 11/08/2027), which is the authority for CCSP and SOURCE, including Alternative Living Services in licensed personal care homes. Waivers do not pay room and board.
- 21st Century Cures Act (EVV), implemented by DCH. Georgia uses Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Applicable claims with dates of service on or after Sept 14, 2026 must go through EVV. **Whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself is unverified; confirm with DCH.**
- Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators - Application for Initial Licensure as ALC or PCH Administrator (form dated 11.2022). Confirm the current fee before relying on it.

**Items to verify before use**
- The PCH staffing ratio (1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and per 25 in non-waking hours) comes from third-party-hosted text. It is **not confirmed** against current official text. Verify it with DCH before using it.
- Several retrieved rule texts were truncated (including the full lists in .07, and paragraphs of .13, .15, .16, .21, .25 and .29). Read the full current text of each rule before finalizing the manual.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD)** | Permits and licenses PCHs and ALCs; conducts unannounced periodic inspections; issues memory care certificates | pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov; https://dch.georgia.gov/divisionsoffices/hfrd/facilities-provider-information/personal-care-homes |
| **DCH Office of Health Planning (OHP)** | Issues the Letter of Determination required with the initial ALC application | https://dch.georgia.gov/con-applications-and-forms |
| **Georgia State Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators (Secretary of State)** | Licenses ALC administrators and administrators of 25+ bed PCHs | 404-424-9966 |
| **DCH Division of Medicaid (Medical Assistance Plans)** | Administers the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP and SOURCE) and contracts with the 12 Area Agencies on Aging | https://medicaid.georgia.gov/programs/all-programs/waiver-programs |
| **Area Agencies on Aging** | First point of contact for waiver assessment and screening | 866-552-4464 (866-55-AGING) |
| **Georgia DHS Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS)** | Determines Medicaid financial eligibility for the waiver program and keeps the EDWP waiting list | https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/medicaid/2131/ |
| **Georgia DHS Division of Aging Services** | Sets the monthly PCH room-and-board rate for SOURCE residents | https://www.georgiahealth.us/medicaid-waivers/ |
| **State Fire Marshal** | Fire safety inspection report (no violations, capacity load) dated within 12 months of application | See the DCH ALC application packet |
| **Georgia Medicaid GAMMIS provider enrollment** | Medicaid provider enrollment and revalidation; retroactive enrollment is not permitted | https://www.mmis.georgia.gov/portal/ |
| **Georgia Department of Labor** | State unemployment insurance registration and tax rates | https://dol.georgia.gov/faqs-employers/employers-faqs-unemployment-insurance |
| **Local zoning and planning officials** | Applicant must address local zoning and location requirements | Contact your local jurisdiction |
| **State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program** (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.) | Resident advocacy. The assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone must be posted in a common area (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.25) | Insert local ombudsman contact: [OMBUDSMAN NAME / PHONE] |

Phone numbers for DCH HFRD and the other agencies not listed above were not available when this manual was prepared. Add them from the agency websites.

### Official policy checklist and application documents

Georgia has **no single DCH policy-review form** for PCHs or ALCs. DCH reviews this manual against the following official documents:

1. **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)**, Owner Governance, paragraph (2): the list of required policies and procedures (items (a) through (p)) for Assisted Living Communities of 25 or more residents. Issued by DCH HFRD and published by the Georgia Secretary of State.
2. **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07(3)**, Governing Body, paragraph (3): the list of required policies and procedures (items (a) through (p)) for Personal Care Homes of 2–24 beds. The PCH list is not identical to the ALC list. It differs in order and wording; for example, the staffing plan appears last as item (p) in the PCH list, and the ALC list adds the certified medication aide reference in (h).
3. **DCH Assisted Living Community Application Checklist**, including the **Affidavit of Compliance for Ch. 111-8-63** and the Affidavit of Financial Stability.
4. **DCH Personal Care Home Application Checklist**, including the **Affidavit of Compliance for Ch. 111-8-62**.

Both lists are stated as a **minimum**. Other sections of ch. 111-8-62 and 111-8-63 contain further written-policy or program requirements, such as resident rights, memory care and staff training, and this manual addresses them as well.

The application checklists contain only application paperwork (14 items for PCH, 15 for ALC). They do not ask for the manual to be uploaded. Instead, the applicant signs the notarized Affidavit of Compliance, and DCH reviews the policies for sufficiency and compliance during unannounced inspections. Deficient policies may bring sanctions under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-25. The checklist pages carry no revision dates, so re-check the DCH page before relying on them.

**Appendix A** maps every official item, each lettered paragraph of .07(2) or .07(3) and each related rule requirement, to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to show an inspector where each requirement is met.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize.** Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and bracketed field, and remove content that applies to the other license type.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and document it.
- **Keep current.** Review it at least annually and whenever a rule, form or operation changes. Confirm the current text on the Georgia Secretary of State rules site and the DCH website.
- **Train.** All staff must be trained on the manual, with signed acknowledgments and training records kept, and retrained when it changes.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Assisted Living Communities (rule index .01-.34)
citations.requirement: Minimum standards for personal care homes licensed as assisted living communities (ALC, 25+ residents). The Secretary of State page and Cornell index list rules .01-.34, including .08 Community Leadership, .09 Workforce, .14 Emergency Preparedness, .19 Memory Care, .20 Medications, .26 Change in Condition, .29 Discharge and .30 Reports.

citations.title: Personal Care Homes (rules .01-.09 text retrieved)
citations.requirement: Governs personal care homes (2+ unrelated adults). Legal authority is O.C.G.A. Title 31, Chapters 2 and 7. A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license. The rules are mirrored for PCHs in the Secretary of State text; only .01-.06 were read in full here.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the policies must use. Examples: abuse; injury (includes pressure ulcers not properly cared for); assistive device (needs a physician/NP/PA order, a written care plan and resident consent); assisted self-preservation; chemical and physical restraints (bedrails, wheelchair safety bars, tight tucking and mitts count; alarm wristbands do not); limited nursing services (care completed within 7 days or intermittently); memory care center; medical alert system (DCH-approved); proxy caregiver; Mattie's-call-related elopement; owner (10% or more interest).

citations.title: Application for Permit
citations.requirement: The governing body applies on DCH forms. DCH will not act on an incomplete application or one without fees (per Ch. 111-8-25). Required: floor plan with window, door, common-area and room measurements plus .jpg photos; administrator or on-site manager name; full ownership disclosure (10%+ owners and registered agent); ownership or lease documentation; local zoning addressed with local officials; initial application must include a CPA financial stability affidavit (going concern for 2 years).

citations.title: Permits
citations.requirement: Valid permit required before admitting residents. Permit displayed conspicuously where residents and visitors see it. Not transferable. Must be returned and is no longer valid if the community moves to an unlicensed location, ownership changes, or the permit is suspended or revoked. Separate permit for each premises. May not exceed licensed capacity on the permit face. Must disclose ALC licensure classification in marketing. No other business may operate on the premises in a way that intrudes on residents' quiet enjoyment.

citations.title: Owner Governance
citations.requirement: The community must have a functioning governing body that oversees compliance with Ch. 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100. The governing body implements policies supporting dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy. Policies must at minimum direct staff and residents on: (a) services available, including memory care and proxy caregivers; (b) a staffing plan under which ratios rise as assisted-self-preservation residents increase; (c) admissions, discharges and immediate transfers that avoid admitting or retaining residents needing more care than the community is authorized or able to provide; (d) refunds on transfer or discharge; (e) staff training and evaluation; (f) house rules and enforcement; plus further items through investigation and reporting (list truncated in retrieved text; read the full paragraph before finalizing).

citations.title: Workforce Qualifications, Training and Staffing (amended eff. May 21, 2025)
citations.requirement: Full text read. (1) On-site manager and responsible staff 21+; no staff under 18 without line-of-sight supervision (17-year-old exception for a GA high-school nursing-assistant track). (2) All-staff training within 60 days. (3) Hands-on staff training within 60 days, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration. (4) At least 2 trained staff present at all times, one per occupied floor. (5) 24 CE hours in year one; (6) 16 hours annually after. (7) Training records. (10) TB screening and physical within 12 months before providing care. (11)-(13) Criminal background checks under Ch. 111-8-12. (14)-(15) Employment history; personnel files kept 3 years after departure. (17) No impairment on duty. (18) Average monthly ratio 1:15 awake waking hours and 1:20 non-waking for minimal-need residents; at least 2 direct care staff 24/7, one per occupied floor; RN or LPN on site 8 h/wk (1-30 residents), 16 (31-60), 24 (61-90), 40 (90+). (19) Sufficient staff time. (21) Staffing plans and schedules kept 1 year. (22) ID badges. (23) Medical alert system requirements.

citations.title: Community Accountability
citations.requirement: Records available to DCH inspectors. Inspection report disputes due within 10 days of receipt. Written plan of correction due within 10 days, with date-certain actions. Most recent inspection report and plan of correction displayed where residents and visitors see them. Website link to the previous 18 months of reports and plans if the community has a website. Keep an accurate licensed residential care profile. Services and marketing must match the license, profile and rules. Only a licensed ALC may hold itself out as offering assisted living care. No memory care center without a current certificate.

citations.title: Community Furnishings
citations.requirement: Furnishings maintained intact and functional. Name plate outside each resident's room unless declined. Closet or wardrobe and reading-adequate lighting in each room. Individual bed at least 36 x 72 inches with mattress at least 5 inches thick (4 if synthetic). No cots, roll-aways, double-decks, stacked bunks, hide-a-beds or studio couches in lieu of beds. Linens for residents needing linen service: at minimum 2 sheets, pillow, pillowcase, blanket, bedspread, towels and washcloth. Help hanging pictures. (Only some paragraphs were visible in the retrieved text.)

citations.title: Community Safety Precautions
citations.requirement: Interior and exterior kept clean, in good repair and free of unsafe conditions. Entrances, exits, sidewalks and escape routes kept free of hazards. Name and house number visible from the street. (Only (1), (11) and (12) were visible; fire drill and other paragraphs were not retrieved.)

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: Comply with Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans). Post evacuation maps with marked escape routes on each floor. Keep a clear accessible emergency route through common areas. The disaster plan is readily accessible to staff, residents and families and names the staff positions responsible for implementing it and obtaining emergency medical attention. Give timely notice of the relocation address to residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH if an emergency forces relocation.

citations.title: Admission and Resident Retention
citations.requirement: (1) Admission profile: age 18+; no active TB; no need for continuous medical or nursing care; no need for physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control; able to actively participate in transfers; able to participate in social and leisure activities. (2) The administrator or on-site manager must document the evaluation of applicants, including a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and documented added safety measures for registered sex offenders or violent offenders. A physician examination on DCH forms is referenced. (4) Community admission decisions (text truncated in retrieved copy).

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Plain-language agreement consistent with the licensed residential care profile. Must state all fees and what they cover. Written notice at least 30 days before any increase in personal-service charges and at least 60 days before any increase in room-and-board charges. Provisions for continuous assessment and referral or transfer on change of condition. A description of the complaint process. Transportation provisions, with emergency transport available at all times. A refund policy on death, transfer or discharge. Further items follow (truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: Services in the Community
citations.requirement: (1) Provide assisted living including protective care and watchful oversight. (2) Resident needs assessment covering family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and preferences. (3) Written care plan within 14 days of admission, updated at least annually and when needs change substantially or on assignment to a memory care center. (4) Daily social activities. (6) Operable non-pay telephone for staff emergency use and private resident access. (7) Do not restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident into or out of the bedroom. (8) Proxy caregiver options. (11) Periodic or short-term medical and nursing health services are not provided as community services; they are purchased by the resident (care planning, training, medication administration and competency checks excepted).

citations.title: Additional Requirements for Certified Memory Care Centers
citations.requirement: Applies if the community holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care or charges more for it. The licensed residential care profile must carry a written description with 12 elements (philosophy, how services differ, staffing and training, admission and screening criteria, assessment and reassessment triggers before the customary quarterly review, staffing patterns, physical environment and security, activities, fees, discharge criteria, emergency procedures, family involvement). Staffing: one dementia-trained direct care staff per 12 residents in waking hours and per 15 in non-waking hours (monthly average). RN or LPN hours in the center: 8 h/wk (1-12 residents), 16 (13-30), 24 (31-40), 40 (more than 40). Annual staff training. Physical design paragraph (b) not read.

citations.title: Medications
citations.requirement: Full text read. Residents capable of self-administration may keep and self-administer medications securely. Staff assistance is limited to listed tasks for unit or multi-dose packaged medications, including EpiPen use under a written protocol with a 911 call. Only certified medication aides (CMAs) may administer. The community must check the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry, run skills competency checks, use an RN or pharmacist for quarterly random observations, and have a pharmacist do quarterly drug regimen reviews. An RN, pharmacist or physician does annual competency reviews. Orders are required for all medications including OTC. New prescriptions within 48 hours and MAR updated within 48 hours. Daily MAR. Medications stored under lock and key; controlled substances in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction with a daily-updated log; duplicate keys on site; original containers; disposal per FDA/EPA guidance; liquid morphine limited to 50 ml per hospice patient.

citations.title: Nutrition and Food Preparation
citations.requirement: At least 3 regularly scheduled well-balanced meals per day, 7 days a week, plus therapeutic diets as ordered by the resident's healthcare provider. No more than 14 hours between the evening and morning meals. Nutrition per Recommended Daily Diet Allowances. At least one nutritious snack offered daily. Food must be clean, wholesome and safe. Menus dated and planned at least 1 week ahead for regular and therapeutic diets, posted or easily available, with resident input encouraged. Perishables held at or below 41 degrees F. A third-party reproduction states menus as served are kept 30 days. Only some paragraphs were visible.

citations.title: Residents' Files
citations.requirement: The administrator or on-site manager keeps an individual file for each resident. Confidential; disclosed only to the resident, representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents and those with written authorization. Available for inspection and copying by the resident or representative and by DCH. Contents include: identifying information; physician, hospital and pharmacy of choice; record of monetary transactions with itemized receipts; record and receipt of valuables held in safekeeping; health information (appraisals, diagnoses, diets, medications, orders); inventory of personal valuables; signed Resident's Rights form; signed admission agreement; powers of attorney; living will, DPOA-HC or Georgia advance directive (forms available at admission); signed end-of-life medical orders.

citations.title: Supporting Residents Rights and Obtaining Feedback
citations.requirement: Rights cannot be waived except by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow. Care must be adequate and appropriate. No punishment or harassment for enforcing rights. Rights to vote, choose activities and schedules, interact with the community, and privacy in the room (staff knock first). Free and private communication without staff censorship. Married residents may share a room, and no more than two residents may share a bedroom. Freedom from coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community. (u) A resident without a court commitment or authorized representative may self-discharge on 30 days written notice. (v) Access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.), with the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone posted in a common area. Paragraphs on feedback were not retrieved.

citations.title: Procedures for Change in Resident's Condition
citations.requirement: Full text read. On an accident or sudden adverse change the community acts immediately, notifies the representative or legal surrogate, and records the change and response in the resident file. For an unresponsive resident: hospice enrollee, call the hospice, then the health care agent, then EMS and CPR if no DNR. Valid DNR: honor it in good faith. Health care agent under O.C.G.A. 31-32-1 et seq.: call the agent, and if unavailable with no DNR call EMS and start CPR. No hospice, DNR or directive: call EMS and start CPR unless clearly futile and no physician, authorized RN or PA is on site. Staff need ready access to emergency numbers and resident information, including during transport. The administrator or on-site manager must start an immediate investigation of the cause of an accident, injury or death, report to the representative or legal surrogate, and keep copies in the resident file and a central quality-assurance file.

citations.title: Discharge or Transfer of Residents
citations.requirement: (1) Each admission agreement includes a written procedure for discharge and transfer. The administrator or on-site manager contacts the representative or legal surrogate when discharge or transfer is needed. The community gives 30 days written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required. Later paragraphs not retrieved.

citations.title: Reports to the Department
citations.requirement: Full text read. Call local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing (Mattie's Call Act). Report the start and end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement. Report serious incidents to DCH within 24 hours of the incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred: accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness; serious injury needing medical attention; rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation (Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act); external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation; an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record. Report contents: community and administrator names, incident date and discovery date, incident type and brief description, immediate corrective or preventive action. DCH may open a separate complaint investigation.

citations.title: Application for Permit (PCH)
citations.requirement: PCH application on DCH format with truthful disclosure. Sketch or drawing of the home and grounds showing windows, doors, room measurements and bed placement, plus ownership or lease documentation. Administrator or on-site manager name before the permit issues. Disclosure of owners with 10% or more and the registered agent. Local zoning addressed. A CPA financial stability affidavit is required for an initial application of 25 or more beds. No PCH may operate and no resident may be admitted without a current permit. No memory care center may operate without a current certificate.

citations.title: Permits (PCH)
citations.requirement: Valid permit before operating. Permit displayed conspicuously. May not exceed approved licensed capacity. Permit invalid and returned when the home ceases to operate, moves, or ownership changes (text truncated after this point in the retrieved copy).

citations.title: Governing Body (PCH)
citations.requirement: The governing body oversees compliance with Title 31 Ch. 7, and DCH Ch. 111-8-25, 111-8-62 and 111-8-100. It keeps DCH supplied with current contact information (name, email for notices, physical addresses, phones for the governing body and administrator or on-site manager) and makes staff accountable for delivering notices to it. Required policies cover services, admissions/discharges/immediate transfers, refunds, staff training and evaluation, house rules, rights, and medication management (list continues; truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: PCH Administrator Qualifications
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: for fewer than 25 beds, an associate's degree, or a GED/high school diploma plus 2 years' licensed PCH or healthcare experience, and age 21+. For 25+ beds, a valid Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license within 60 days of hire.

citations.title: PCH Workforce Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: on-site managers and responsible staff persons 21+; under-18 staff only under line-of-sight supervision; new staff work-related training including emergency first aid and CPR certification within 60 days.

citations.title: Definitions (PCH)
citations.requirement: Legal surrogate definition: no member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family members, may serve as a resident's legal surrogate. A copy of any power of attorney must be kept in the resident file. Also defines abuse, exploitation, physical and chemical restraint, memory care center, representative, and similar terms.

citations.title: Operation of memory care center; certificate required; staffing and training requirements
citations.requirement: Memory care centers: all staff get at least 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation within the first 30 days. Direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of dementia training within the first 30 days of working independently with dementia residents, then at least 8 hours annually. Keep documentation of course content, instructor qualifications, agendas and attendance rosters.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Services Available in the Community (Personal Services, Assisted Living Care, Memory Care, Proxy Caregivers)
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), all staff, residents, representatives and prospective residents
policies.purpose: To state clearly which services [AGENCY NAME] provides, which it does not provide, and which a resident may purchase from outside providers. This ensures that what we say, advertise and deliver matches our license, our licensed residential care profile and the Rules of the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH).
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(a) (ALC .07(2)(a)): the services available in the assisted living community, including personal services, assisted living care, memory care services and any other specialized services such as memory care centers and designated proxy caregivers.

[AGENCY NAME] is licensed by DCH as an assisted living community. It provides assisted living, including protective care and watchful oversight, under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.17(1). Each resident receives personal services, such as help with bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, mobility, eating and medication assistance. Services are based on a written needs assessment and care plan. The assessment covers family supports, ADL function, physical care needs, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and the resident's preferences. The care plan is written within 14 days of admission. It is updated at least annually, when the resident's needs change substantially, and on assignment to a memory care center. The community provides daily social activities. It also provides an operable non-pay telephone for staff emergency use and private telephone access for residents.

Periodic or short-term medical and nursing health services are not community services. The resident or representative purchases them from a qualified outside provider. The exceptions, which the community does provide, are care planning, staff training, medication administration and competency checks. The community does not admit or keep residents who need continuous medical or nursing care, or who need physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control. The community does not lock a resident into or out of a bedroom and does not restrict free access to common areas.

An assistive device is used only with a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant order, a written care plan and the resident's consent.

Memory care: [AGENCY NAME] [DOES / DOES NOT] operate a memory care center. If it does, the center operates only while a current DCH memory care certificate is in effect. Our licensed residential care profile then carries the required written description of memory care services. We do not describe any area as memory care, dementia care or secured dementia care unless the certificate is current. Staffing, training and design requirements for the center are in ALC-04, HLT-02 and ALC-02.

Proxy caregivers: [AGENCY NAME] [DOES / DOES NOT] use designated proxy caregivers under Ch. 111-8-100. If it does, proxy caregivers perform only the tasks, and only for the residents, that the permit, the resident's written consent and the proxy caregiver training allow. See ALC-13 and ALC-14.

Only a licensed ALC may hold itself out as offering assisted living care. All brochures, website text, tours and admission discussions must match the license, the licensed residential care profile and the rules. The administrator keeps the profile accurate and reviews it whenever services, pricing, staffing or memory care status change.

definitions.definition: Protective care and watchful oversight, with personal services, provided by a licensed assisted living community as defined in Ch. 111-8-63.
Direct help with activities of daily living, such as bathing, dressing, toileting, mobility, eating and grooming, plus medication assistance as the rules allow.
Nursing care that is completed within 7 days or that is needed only intermittently. Under Rule .03 and .17(11) it is purchased by the resident and is not a community-provided service.
A distinct unit or community that holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care, or charges more for it, and that has a current DCH memory care certificate.
A person designated under Ch. 111-8-100 and trained to perform specific health-related tasks for a resident, as the rules allow.
The DCH-filed description of the community's services, staffing, fees and (if applicable) memory care program. It must be accurate and consistent with marketing.
A device that needs a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant order, a written care plan and resident consent before use (Rule .03).

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], maintains a written Schedule of Services listing every personal service, the assisted living care, social activity, transportation and any memory care or proxy caregiver service the community provides. The Schedule is attached to each admission agreement.

Before the license is issued and whenever services change, the Administrator compares the Schedule of Services, the marketing materials and the licensed residential care profile line by line. Any mismatch is corrected before use. The review is dated and signed.

Marketing staff and tour guides use only approved scripts and printed materials. The Administrator reviews every new brochure, website page and advertisement against the license before it is released.

During pre-admission screening (see ALC-03 and ADM-01), the Administrator or on-site manager explains verbally and in writing what the community does and does not provide. This includes that periodic or short-term medical and nursing services are purchased by the resident from outside providers.

Within the admission process, a qualified staff member completes the needs assessment covering family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and preferences.

The care plan is written within 14 days of admission with the resident and the representative or legal surrogate. It is signed and filed in the resident file. It is updated at least annually, when needs change substantially, and when a resident is assigned to a memory care center.

Staff provide only services listed in the care plan and the Schedule of Services. A staff member who sees a need not covered by the plan reports it to the on-site manager that shift. The manager initiates a reassessment (see ADM-02).

When a resident needs a limited nursing service, the on-site manager helps the resident or representative arrange it from the resident's chosen provider (for example a home health agency). The service is recorded in the care plan. Community staff do not perform that service unless the rules allow it.

Before any assistive device is used, the on-site manager confirms there is a written order from a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant, a written care plan entry and the resident's signed consent. These are filed in the resident file.

If the community has a memory care center, the Administrator confirms the DCH certificate is current each month and posts or files it as DCH requires. If the certificate lapses or is not renewed, admissions to the center stop immediately and the Administrator notifies DCH and affected representatives. Residents are not described as memory care residents until a certificate is in place.

If the community uses proxy caregivers, the Administrator confirms before each assignment that the proxy caregiver has completed Ch. 111-8-100 training, that the resident or representative has consented in writing, and that the task is within the permit. The assignment is documented in the care plan.
Staff ensure daily social activities are offered, a non-pay telephone is working for staff emergencies, and residents can use a phone privately. Staff check the telephone weekly and log the result.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually and whenever DCH amends Ch. 111-8-63 or the profile changes. The review is documented in the governing body minutes (see GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Adopt this policy, approve the Schedule of Services and ensure the community does not offer services outside its license or certificate.

Keep the licensed residential care profile, Schedule of Services and marketing consistent. Confirm memory care certification and proxy caregiver authority. Screen applicants against what the community can provide.
Oversee assessments and care plans, assistive device approvals and arrangement of purchased nursing services. Report mismatches between needs and services.
Deliver only the services in the care plan. Report unmet needs or changes to the manager immediately.
Describe services accurately using approved materials. Do not promise services the community does not offer.

documentation: Schedule of Services with revision dates
Licensed residential care profile and annual comparison checklist
Marketing material review log
Resident needs assessment and signed care plan (14-day, annual and change-in-condition updates)
Assistive device orders, care plan entries and resident consents
DCH memory care certificate and monthly verification log, if applicable
Proxy caregiver training records, written consents and care plan entries, if applicable
Telephone check log

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staffing Plan and Ratios That Rise With Assisted Self-Preservation Needs
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), Administrator, on-site manager, scheduler and all direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always has enough trained staff on duty to meet residents' needs and to evacuate residents safely. Staffing rises as the number of residents who need help to reach safety (assisted self-preservation) increases.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(b) (ALC .07(2)(b)): the staffing plan that the community utilizes to ensure that staffing ratios increase proportionally as the number of residents who require assisted self-preservation increases.

Minimum floor (never reduced): at least 2 trained direct care staff are on site 24 hours a day whenever residents are present, with at least 1 on each occupied floor (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09(4) and (18)). A new hire still inside the 60-day training window does not count toward the 2 fully trained staff.

Baseline ratios: for residents with minimal needs, the monthly average is at least 1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents during waking hours and 1 per 20 during non-waking hours.

Proportional increase: [AGENCY NAME] counts each resident who needs assisted self-preservation as 1.5 residents when calculating the required number of direct care staff. The staffing plan is recalculated whenever the number of such residents changes, and at least weekly. The Administrator may set staffing higher than this formula. Staffing is never set below the rule minimums. Direct care staff counted toward the ratio are not assigned duties that take them away from residents (for example, kitchen or laundry duty).

Example: a 60-resident community with 12 assisted-self-preservation residents has a weighted count of 48 + (12 x 1.5) = 66. At 1 per 15 awake, that is 4.4, so the schedule provides 5 direct care staff on waking hours. At 1 per 20, that is 3.3, so it provides 4 on non-waking hours, and always at least 1 on each occupied floor.

Licensed nurse hours: an RN or LPN is on site at least 8 hours per week for 1-30 residents, 16 hours for 31-60, 24 hours for 61-90, and 40 hours for more than 90 residents (Rule .09(18)). Staff time must be sufficient to meet residents' needs as written in their care plans. Staffing plans and schedules are kept for at least 1 year (Rule .09(21)). If the community operates a memory care center, its separate staffing and nurse-hour requirements apply (see ALC-01, ALC-04 and HLT-02).

The plan also covers relief staff and the absence of regularly scheduled staff, so the minimums are met on every shift.

definitions.definition: As defined in Rule .03. In practice, a resident who needs staff help or prompting to reach safety in an emergency such as a fire.
The hours residents are normally awake and active, set in the written staffing plan. Non-waking hours are the remaining overnight hours.
Staff who have completed the all-staff and hands-on training required within 60 days of hire, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration.
The community's planning count: minimal-need residents count as 1 each and assisted-self-preservation residents as 1.5 each.
Total direct care staff hours worked in the period divided by resident days, calculated for waking and non-waking hours separately.

procedures: On the first business day of each month, the Administrator or designee lists every resident and classifies each as minimal need or assisted self-preservation, based on the current assessment and care plan. The list is signed and dated.

The Administrator calculates the weighted resident count and the number of direct care staff needed in waking and non-waking hours. Results are written into the Staffing Plan, which also shows required staff per occupied floor.

The scheduler builds a weekly schedule from the Staffing Plan. Each shift shows at least 2 trained direct care staff on site, at least 1 on each occupied floor, and the name and training status of each.
The scheduler marks any employee within 60 days of hire as 'in training' and does not count that person toward the 2 fully trained staff.

The on-site manager reports every change in resident acuity (new assisted-self-preservation resident, hospital return, change in mobility or cognition) to the Administrator within 24 hours. The Administrator recalculates the weighted count and adds shifts the same week if needed.

The Administrator schedules RN or LPN hours at or above the required weekly minimum for the current census band. The nurse signs a time record showing hours and tasks (assessments, care planning, training, medication oversight).

At each shift change, the outgoing and incoming lead staff confirm the minimum staff and per-floor coverage and sign the shift log. If coverage would drop below the minimum, the lead calls the on-call supervisor immediately.

Absences: the scheduler keeps a current list of relief and on-call staff. When a call-off occurs, the scheduler calls relief staff in order. If the minimum cannot be filled, the Administrator or on-site manager works the floor or arranges coverage by a fully trained person. Staff do not leave until relieved.

If an emergency leaves one floor without a trained staff member, the lead notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator documents the cause, the time and the corrective action, and reviews it with the governing body.
Staff must not work while impaired, and a staff member who may be impaired is removed from duty at once and replaced. See ALC-10.

At month end, the Administrator calculates the monthly average ratio from actual hours worked for waking and non-waking periods. If the result is below the baseline or the weighted target, the Administrator adds staff hours the next month and records the reason.
Each quarter, the Quality Assurance Committee reviews call-offs, vacancies, overtime, resident incidents and complaints in relation to staffing. Findings are recorded in the QA file (see ALC-12).
Staffing plans, posted schedules, shift logs and time records are kept for at least 1 year and are available to DCH inspectors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Fund the staffing plan and require the Administrator to staff above the minimum when resident needs rise.
Classify residents, recalculate the weighted count, approve the schedule, verify nurse hours and the monthly average and review staffing quarterly.
Build compliant schedules, track training status, fill absences and keep records.
Confirm coverage each shift, report acuity changes within 24 hours and escalate shortfalls.
Be on site for the required hours and document them.
Remain at assigned post and floor, report call-offs promptly and not leave until relieved.

documentation: Monthly resident classification list
Written Staffing Plan with weighted calculations
Weekly schedules showing staff, floor and training status
Shift logs and coverage confirmations
RN/LPN time records
Monthly average ratio calculations
Call-off and relief records
QA review notes. All staffing plans and schedules are kept at least 1 year.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Admissions, Discharges, Immediate Transfers and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), Administrator, on-site manager, admissions staff, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To admit only people whose needs the community is authorized and able to meet, to retain residents only while that remains true, to carry out discharges and emergency transfers safely and lawfully, and to return money fairly and promptly when a resident leaves or dies.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(c) (ALC .07(2)(c)): admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the community does not admit or retain residents who need more care than the assisted living community is authorized or capable of providing. It also meets 111-8-63-.07(2)(d) (ALC .07(2)(d)): refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged.

Admission profile (Rule .15(1)). [AGENCY NAME] admits a person only if the person is 18 or older; does not have active tuberculosis; does not need continuous medical or nursing care; does not need physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control; can actively participate in transfers; and can participate in social and leisure activities. The Administrator or on-site manager personally documents the evaluation of each applicant. That includes a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check. If the applicant is a registered sex offender or has a violent offense history, added safety measures are documented before any admission decision. Admission decisions also consider a physician's examination on the DCH form.

Retention. A resident is not kept if the resident's needs go beyond what the community is authorized or able to provide. Fit is reviewed at every reassessment and whenever a change in condition occurs.

Discharge and transfer (Rule .29(1)). Each admission agreement contains a written discharge and transfer procedure. When discharge or transfer is needed, the Administrator or on-site manager contacts the representative or legal surrogate. The community gives 30 days' written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required. Emergencies and sudden changes are handled under Rule .26 and HLT-01. A resident may also self-discharge on 30 days' written notice as provided in ALC-06.

Refunds (Rule .16). The admission agreement states the refund policy on death, transfer or discharge. [AGENCY NAME] refunds all unused prepaid personal-service and room-and-board charges, prorated by the day from the day after the resident moves out or dies, plus any deposit, less only documented charges owed under the agreement. Refunds are paid within 30 days of the move-out or death to the resident, representative, legal surrogate or estate. The refund calculation is given in writing.

definitions.definition: An emergency move of a resident to a hospital or higher level of care when the resident's condition or behavior creates imminent danger that the community cannot safely manage, without waiting for the 30-day notice period.
The ending of a resident's stay at the community, whether at the community's initiative, the resident's choice, or because of death.
A person with legal authority to act for the resident, such as a health care agent or guardian.
Return of prepaid fees and deposits not yet earned by the community, as stated in the admission agreement.
A check of the national registry of sex offenders, run for each applicant and documented in the file.

procedures: On first inquiry, the admissions staff gives the applicant and family the Schedule of Services, price list, admission agreement and the retention limits in this policy. The applicant is told the community cannot admit or keep people who need continuous nursing care or restraints.

Before admission, the Administrator or on-site manager gathers the physician's examination on the DCH form, current medication and diet orders, and the applicant's health history. The document is reviewed for any active TB or need for continuous nursing care.

The Administrator or on-site manager meets or speaks with the applicant and representative, and evaluates the applicant against each point of the admission profile (age 18+, no active TB, no continuous nursing, no restraints, able to take part in transfers and activities). The evaluation is written, dated and signed.

The Administrator runs a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry (or arranges a fingerprint check) for every applicant before admission. If a registry hit or violent offense history appears, the Administrator documents added safety measures (for example room placement, supervision and notification of the Quality Assurance Committee) before deciding.

The Administrator makes the admission decision. If the applicant needs more care than the community is authorized or able to provide, the Administrator declines and gives the applicant a written explanation and referral suggestions within 2 business days.

If admitted, the Administrator reviews the admission agreement in plain language with the resident and representative, including fees, the refund policy, the 30-day discharge notice and the complaint process. Signed copies are given to the resident and filed.

At every reassessment and within 24 hours of any change in condition, the on-site manager compares the resident's current needs to the admission profile and to what the community can provide. If a gap appears, the manager notifies the Administrator the same day.

When the Administrator concludes the community can no longer meet a resident's needs, the Administrator contacts the representative or legal surrogate promptly. Together with the resident, physician and, where relevant, the case manager or ombudsman, they plan the transfer to an appropriate setting.

The Administrator delivers 30 days' written notice of intent to discharge or transfer, stating the reason, the effective date and how to complain. The notice is given to the resident and representative, and a copy goes to the file. The full process is in ADM-03.

Immediate transfer: if a resident's condition or behavior creates imminent danger or requires care the community cannot provide, staff act at once. They call 911 if needed, notify the representative or legal surrogate and the physician, and send current medication lists, face sheet and advance directive or DNR status with the resident. Staff handle unresponsive residents under HLT-01 and Rule .26. The Administrator documents the reason the transfer could not wait for 30 days.

Within 24 hours after an immediate transfer, the Administrator contacts the receiving facility, confirms the resident's arrival and condition and records the contact. The community decides about readmission only after reassessment against the admission profile.

The business office calculates any refund within 5 business days of the move-out or death. It prorates prepaid charges by the day, adds back any deposit and deducts only documented amounts owed. It prepares a written statement showing each step of the calculation, which the Administrator reviews and signs.

The refund and statement are sent to the resident, representative, legal surrogate or estate within 30 days of move-out or death. A copy of the check and statement is kept in the resident file and the business office file. Property and funds held for the resident are returned under RR-03 at the same time.
The Administrator reviews every discharge and transfer quarterly with the Quality Assurance Committee to identify admission screening gaps (see ALC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Decide admissions, document evaluations and registry inquiries, issue discharge notices, review immediate transfers and approve refunds.
Perform or assist with evaluations, monitor fit at reassessment, coordinate transfers and notify representatives.
Give accurate information, collect required documents and never promise services outside the profile.
Calculate and issue refunds timely, with written statements.
Support decisions to decline or discharge when needs exceed the community's authority or ability.

documentation: Applicant evaluation signed by the Administrator or on-site manager
Physician's examination on the DCH form
National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint results and added safety measures
Signed admission agreement
Written declination letters
30-day discharge/transfer notices and proof of delivery
Immediate transfer documentation and receiving-facility contact notes
Refund calculation, statement and proof of payment
Quarterly discharge/transfer review minutes

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Training and Ongoing Evaluation (Including Memory Care and Proxy Caregiver Training)
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), Administrator, on-site manager, all employees, and proxy caregivers if used
policies.purpose: To ensure every person working at [AGENCY NAME] is trained before and after they begin working with residents, that training is documented, and that each employee's performance is evaluated regularly.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(e) (ALC .07(2)(e)): training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered.

General training (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09). All staff are trained within 60 days of hire. Each employee receives a copy of the Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act during initial training. Hands-on staff also complete first aid and CPR with return demonstration within 60 days of hire. Hands-on staff, including the administrator, complete 24 hours of continuing education in the first year and 16 hours each year after. Training records are kept for each employee.

Qualifications and health. The on-site manager and staff in charge are at least 21. No employee under 18 works without line-of-sight supervision, subject to the high-school nursing-assistant exception in the rule. Every employee has a TB screening and a physical within 12 months before providing care, and a criminal background check as described in STF-01. No employee may work while impaired.

Memory care. If memory care is offered, all staff complete at least 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation within their first 30 days (O.C.G.A. 31-7-12.4). Direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of dementia training within 30 days of working independently with residents who have dementia, and at least 8 hours every year after. The community keeps documentation of course content, instructor qualifications, agendas and attendance rosters.

Proxy caregivers. If designated proxy caregivers are used, each completes the training required by Ch. 111-8-100 before performing any task, and the training is documented.

Evaluation. Every employee receives a written performance evaluation at the end of the 60-day training period and at least annually. Evaluations include direct observation of resident care.

definitions.definition: Staff who provide direct personal care to residents, including the administrator when performing such care.
The trainee performs the skill (for example CPR) while the instructor observes and confirms competence.
Direct care staff who have completed the dementia orientation and dementia training hours required for memory care.
Job-related training hours beyond initial orientation, counted toward the 24-hour first-year and 16-hour annual requirements.
A person trained and designated under Ch. 111-8-100 to perform specific tasks for a resident.

procedures: Before an offer of employment is finalized, the Administrator confirms the candidate meets the age requirements (21+ for on-site manager or staff in charge; no one under 18 without line-of-sight supervision) and has or will complete a background check (see STF-01).
Before the employee provides any care, HR confirms the TB screening and physical were completed within 12 months before care begins, and files proof in the personnel file.

On the first day, the employee is oriented to residents' rights, emergency procedures, fire evacuation and the abuse and neglect reporting duty. The employee signs for a copy of the Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act.

The Administrator or designee assigns a 60-day training checklist to every new employee. The checklist covers all topics the Administrator has set for the employee's role, including infection control, dignity, privacy, communication, resident rights, medication policies and reporting.
Hands-on staff complete first aid and CPR with return demonstration by a qualified instructor within 60 days of hire. The instructor signs a skills sheet.
A new employee works only under supervision of a fully trained staff member until training is complete. The scheduler shows the employee as 'in training' (see ALC-02).

The training coordinator opens a CE record for each hands-on employee. The record tracks 24 hours for year one and 16 hours per year after, with dates, topics, hours, instructor and certificate or sign-in sheet.

The training coordinator reviews CE records monthly and tells each employee and the Administrator in writing when an employee is more than 30 days behind pace. The Administrator schedules makeup training within 30 days.

If memory care is offered, new staff attend at least 4 hours of dementia orientation within the first 30 days. Direct care staff then complete 16 hours of dementia training within 30 days of beginning independent work with residents with dementia, and 8 hours each year after.
For every dementia course, the coordinator files the course outline, instructor qualifications, agenda and signed attendance roster.
If proxy caregivers are used, the Administrator verifies and files proof of Ch. 111-8-100 training before the first assignment. No proxy caregiver works a task they have not been trained on.

Within the 60-day period, the on-site manager or Administrator observes the employee providing care. The manager completes a written evaluation covering competence, attitude, reliability, adherence to policy and resident rights.

Annually, the supervisor completes a written performance evaluation for every employee, reviews it with the employee and obtains the employee's signature. The evaluation identifies training needs for the next year.
When an evaluation or incident shows a skills gap, the supervisor provides retraining within 14 days and documents it. Repeated gaps are handled under ALC-10.
The Administrator reviews the training program each year with the Quality Assurance Committee and updates content to reflect incident trends, resident needs and rule changes.

responsibilities.duty: Make sure training and evaluation occur, approve the curriculum and reports of overdue training and ensure only trained staff are counted toward minimum staffing.
Schedule and track training, file records, observe new staff and conduct evaluations.
Evaluate employees, give feedback and report skills gaps.
Complete training on time, keep certificates and perform duties only after training.
Deliver and document courses, including return demonstrations and dementia content.

documentation: Signed receipt for the Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act
60-day training checklist
First aid and CPR skills sheets
Individual CE records and certificates (24 hrs year one; 16 hrs after)
TB screening and physical
Dementia training records: course content, instructor qualifications, agendas, rosters
Proxy caregiver training records under Ch. 111-8-100, if applicable
60-day and annual written performance evaluations
Retraining records. Personnel and training records are kept 3 years after the employee leaves.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: House Rules and Their Enforcement
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), residents, representatives, visitors and all staff
policies.purpose: To set clear, reasonable house rules that keep the community safe and comfortable for everyone while protecting each resident's rights, dignity and independence, and to apply those rules fairly.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(f) (ALC .07(2)(f)): house rules and their enforcement.

Written house rules are given to every resident and representative before admission and when rules change. House rules never override resident rights. A resident is never punished or harassed for enforcing his or her rights (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.25). House rules may not restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident into or out of the bedroom (Rule .17(7)). No more than two residents may share a bedroom, and married residents may share a room (Rule .25). The community does not allow other businesses to intrude on residents' quiet enjoyment.

Topic rules: Smoking is permitted only in [DESIGNATED SMOKING AREA / NOT PERMITTED], and never in resident rooms, in a way that conflicts with fire safety. Visitors are welcome, subject to reasonable arrangements for safety, privacy and sign-in, which never prevent a resident from seeing visitors the resident chooses. Pets are [PERMITTED UNDER THE PET AGREEMENT / NOT PERMITTED], except service animals. Alcohol use is the resident's choice unless a physician order or the care plan says otherwise, and the community does not sell alcohol.

Enforcement is progressive, respectful and documented. Rules are applied equally to all residents. Rule violations are never answered with threats, loss of services, confinement, restraint or retaliation. Serious or repeated violations that endanger others are handled through care planning, and if necessary, discharge procedures under ALC-03 and ADM-03.

definitions.definition: Written community rules about conduct, safety and shared living that are given to residents and representatives and that may not conflict with the rules of the DCH or resident rights.
The steps staff take to apply house rules, starting with conversation and care planning, in a way that preserves the resident's rights.
Shared spaces such as dining rooms, lounges, hallways and outdoor areas to which residents have free access.
Punishment or harassment of a resident, representative or employee for asserting rights or making a complaint.

procedures: The Administrator, with the governing body, drafts the house rules in plain language and compares each rule against resident rights (ALC-06), fire safety (SAF-03) and Rule .17(7) before approval. The review is documented.
Rules on smoking, visitors, pets and alcohol are written to include their safety reason and any exceptions (service animals, end-of-life visits, physician orders).

Before or at admission, admissions staff gives the house rules to the resident and the representative, explains them, answers questions and obtains a signed acknowledgement. A copy goes in the resident file.
The house rules are posted in a common area along with the ombudsman's name, address and phone number, and the grievance procedure.

When the Administrator changes a rule, the change is written, dated and given to all residents and representatives before it takes effect, with an opportunity to comment. Changes that affect fees follow RR-02 notice periods.
Staff are trained at orientation and annually on the house rules, with emphasis that rules cannot restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident in or out of a bedroom.

When a resident breaks a house rule, the staff member speaks privately and respectfully with the resident, explains the reason for the rule and records the event in the progress notes if it is more than minor.

If a problem repeats, the on-site manager meets with the resident and representative to understand the cause. Behavior may signal pain, confusion or unmet needs. The manager revises the care plan (see ADM-02) and tries solutions that keep the resident's choices.

If a rule violation creates a danger to the resident or others (for example, smoking in a room), the manager takes immediate protective steps such as removing the hazard and increasing supervision, and notifies the Administrator the same day.

The Administrator decides any further action in writing. Fines, loss of privileges, confinement or reduction of services are not used. Where the resident can no longer safely live in the community, discharge follows ALC-03 and ADM-03.
A resident or representative who disagrees with a rule or its enforcement may file a grievance under RR-01 without fear of retaliation. The Administrator responds in writing.
The Administrator reviews rule enforcement events and grievances quarterly with the Quality Assurance Committee and recommends changes to rules that cause conflict or conflict with rights.

responsibilities.duty: Approve house rules and ensure they respect dignity, choice, independence and privacy.
Draft, update and enforce the rules fairly, and prohibit retaliation.
Handle repeat issues, revise care plans and document significant events.
Apply rules respectfully and equally, and never use threats or punishment.
Follow the rules, which are explained to them in writing.

documentation: Approved written house rules with revision dates
Rights-conflict review checklist
Signed resident/representative acknowledgement
Notices of rule changes with dates delivered
Progress notes of significant rule events
Care plan revisions
Grievance records and responses
Quarterly QA review notes

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Protecting Resident Rights
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds), all staff, residents, representatives and legal surrogates
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (HCBS settings, if Medicaid waiver residents are served)
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident of [AGENCY NAME] is treated with dignity and respect and can exercise all the rights set out in Ch. 111-8-63, and that staff know how to protect them.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(g) (ALC .07(2)(g)): protecting the rights of the residents as set forth in these rules.

Rights are explained in the Resident's Rights form, which each resident (or representative or legal surrogate) signs, and which is kept in the resident file (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.24). Rights may be waived only by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow. Staff may not ask a resident to give them up.

The community ensures that: care is adequate and appropriate; residents are not punished or harassed for enforcing their rights; residents may vote; choose their own activities and schedules; interact with the community; and have privacy in their rooms, with staff knocking before entering. Communication is free and private, without staff censorship, including mail, telephone and visitors. Married residents may share a room, and no more than two residents may share a bedroom. Residents are free from coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community. A resident without a court commitment or authorized representative may self-discharge on 30 days' written notice. Residents have access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.). The name, address and phone number of the assigned ombudsman are posted in a common area (Rule .25).

If the community serves Medicaid waiver residents, the setting also respects the federal home and community-based settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)), including privacy, choice and freedom from restraint and coercion.

Grievances are handled under RR-01. Abuse, neglect and exploitation are reported under ALC-09.

definitions.definition: The written statement of rights given to each resident and signed by the resident or the representative, kept in the resident file.
A person authorized by law or by the resident to make decisions on the resident's behalf.
A resident's choice to leave the community, done on 30 days' written notice when no court commitment or authorized representative applies.
A representative of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program who advocates for residents and investigates complaints.
Giving up a right, permitted only by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow.

procedures: At or before admission, the Administrator or on-site manager gives the resident and representative the Resident's Rights form, reads or explains it in plain language, and answers questions. The resident or representative signs. The signed form goes into the resident file.

The Administrator posts, in a common area, the ombudsman's name, address and phone number, the Resident's Rights summary and the grievance procedure. The on-site manager checks monthly that the postings are current and visible.
At hire and annually, every employee is trained on the Resident's Rights and the consequences of violating them. The training is signed and filed (see ALC-04).
Staff knock and wait for a response before entering a resident's room, except in an emergency. Care in a room is provided with the door or curtain closed.
Staff deliver mail unopened and do not read or screen it. Residents may use a private telephone and receive visitors privately. Staff do not listen to calls or review personal communications.
On election days, the on-site manager helps interested residents register, obtain absentee ballots or get to the polls. The help is offered to all residents equally.

Residents choose their daily schedule, meals within menu options, clothing and activities. Staff offer choices and record preferences in the care plan. Staff do not impose a schedule for staff convenience.

The Administrator ensures no staff member or the business office pressures a resident to assign money, valuables or property to the community, to a staff member, or to any person. Gifts and bequests to staff are prohibited. Concerns are reported to the Administrator immediately (see RR-03).
If a married couple wishes to share a room, the Administrator makes arrangements if a suitable room is available. Rooms are never assigned to more than two residents.

If a resident without a court commitment or authorized representative gives 30 days' written notice, the Administrator accepts it, helps plan the move, completes refund calculations under ALC-03 and does not discourage or penalize the resident.

Any staff member who sees or suspects a violation of a resident's rights reports it at once to the on-site manager and Administrator. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are handled under ALC-09. No one is retaliated against for enforcing a right or reporting.
Residents may contact the ombudsman at any time. The community lets the ombudsman meet residents privately and see records the resident consents to or the law allows.
The Administrator reviews rights complaints and observations at the monthly leadership meeting and the quarterly QA review (see ALC-12), and corrects any practice that may limit rights.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt policies that support dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy and hold the Administrator accountable.
Ensure rights are explained, signed forms are filed, ombudsman information is posted and violations are corrected.
Monitor daily practice, postings and resident choice, and respond to concerns.
Respect each resident's rights, report violations and never retaliate.
Exercise rights freely and raise concerns without fear of retaliation.

documentation: Signed Resident's Rights form in each resident file
Ombudsman posting check log
Rights training records for all staff
Written 30-day self-discharge notices and responses
Grievance and rights-violation reports and corrective actions
Records of resident choices in the care plan
QA review minutes on rights issues

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Medication Management, Procurement, Certified Medication Aides and Professional Oversight
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident receives medications safely, accurately and only as ordered. The policy also sets out how medications are obtained, stored, administered and disposed of, who may administer them, and how a nurse, pharmacist or physician oversees that work.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(h) (ALC .07(2)(h) - medication management, procurement, the use of certified medication aides and professional oversight provided for such services). [AGENCY NAME] follows Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.20 in all medication practices. Medication management: residents who are capable of self-administration may keep and take their own medications, stored securely. Staff assistance is limited to the tasks Rule .20 permits for unit-dose or multi-dose packaged medications. Only certified medication aides (CMAs) listed on the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry may administer medications. Procurement: a written order is required for every medication, including over-the-counter products and supplements. New prescriptions are processed and the Medication Administration Record (MAR) is updated within 48 hours. A MAR is kept daily for each resident who receives staff-assisted or administered medications. Professional oversight: a registered nurse (RN) or pharmacist makes quarterly random observations of medication administration. A pharmacist completes a quarterly drug regimen review. An RN, pharmacist or physician completes an annual competency review of each CMA. Storage and disposal: medications are kept under lock and key in their original containers. Controlled substances are kept in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction, with a log updated daily. Duplicate keys are kept on site. Disposal follows FDA and EPA guidance. Liquid morphine is limited to 50 ml per hospice resident.

definitions.definition: An employee who holds current certification on the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry and is the only staff member permitted to administer medications in the community.
A resident's own taking of medications that the resident keeps securely in his or her possession, after the community has determined the resident is capable.
The daily record of each medication order and each dose given, refused or missed, signed by the person who administered it.
A quarterly review of each resident's medications by a pharmacist to identify duplications, interactions, irregularities and the need for prescriber follow-up.
A medication regulated under state or federal law that must be kept in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction with a daily-updated log.
