procedures: Before a CMA works a medication pass, the Administrator or designee checks the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry. A copy of the verification is placed in the personnel file, and the check is repeated at each renewal or on any report of a change in status.

The Administrator verifies that each new CMA completes the hands-on and all-staff training required in Rule .09 within 60 days of hire, and that a skills competency check is completed and documented before the CMA passes medications independently.

Before admission, the Director of Nursing/Nurse Consultant [NURSE NAME] reviews the resident's physician or practitioner orders, and the Administrator confirms each medication, including OTC products and supplements, has a written order.

The Administrator or on-site manager decides with the resident, the physician and the representative whether the resident can safely self-administer. The decision and any limits are recorded in the care plan. A self-administering resident is given a locked space in the room for medications.

For self-administering residents, staff assistance is limited to the tasks Rule .20 lists for unit-dose or multi-dose packaged medications. Staff who are not CMAs do not give, inject or otherwise administer medications. The Administrator posts the permitted-task list in the medication room.

Medications are ordered from [PHARMACY NAME] in unit-dose or multi-dose packaging where available. On the date a new prescription is received, the medication nurse or CMA lead faxes or sends the order to the pharmacy. The new prescription is processed and the MAR is updated within 48 hours of the order.
On receipt of medications, two staff members, one of them a CMA, check each label against the order and the MAR. Any discrepancy goes to the prescriber or pharmacy the same day and is documented.

The CMA gives medications only as ordered, using the five checks (resident, medication, dose, route, time). The CMA initials the MAR at the time each dose is given. Refused, held or missed doses are recorded and reported to the on-site manager, and the prescriber is called when needed.

An EpiPen is used only under a written protocol signed by the resident's prescriber. Staff trained in the protocol give the injection, call 911 immediately, notify the representative and the physician, and document the event.

Medications are stored under lock and key, in original containers, in the medication room or cart. Only CMAs and the Administrator hold keys. Duplicate keys are kept on site in a secure, designated place known to the Administrator and the on-site manager.

Controlled substances are kept in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction. Two staff members count them at each shift change, and the log is updated daily with date, resident, medication, quantity received, given or destroyed, and the signatures of the staff members. Any discrepancy is reported to the Administrator immediately and investigated under ALC-09.
Liquid morphine for a hospice resident is limited to 50 ml per resident. The nurse checks the quantity on hand and coordinates with the hospice agency on supply and disposal.

An RN or pharmacist makes quarterly random observations of medication administration by CMAs and writes up the findings. A pharmacist completes the quarterly drug regimen review, and the Administrator makes sure the prescriber receives and responds to any recommendations.

An RN, pharmacist or physician completes an annual competency review of each CMA. A CMA who does not pass is removed from medication duty until retrained and re-evaluated, and the result is recorded in the personnel file.

Discontinued, expired, contaminated or deceased-resident medications are separated and locked. They are destroyed or disposed of following FDA and EPA guidance by two staff members, who document the medication, quantity, date, method and their signatures.

Every medication error, adverse reaction or omission is reported to the on-site manager and the prescriber immediately. The representative is notified, an incident report is completed, and the event is reviewed in the quality assurance file (see ALC-12). A medication event that results in serious injury is reported under ALC-09.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies CMA registry status, keeps medication policies current, oversees storage and key control, and makes sure quarterly and annual reviews happen on schedule.
Makes quarterly random observations, may perform annual competency reviews, trains staff on protocols such as the EpiPen, and reviews medication events.
Completes quarterly drug regimen reviews, may make quarterly observations and annual competency reviews, and advises on storage and disposal.
Administers medications only as ordered, records each dose on the MAR, maintains the controlled substance log and reports errors immediately.
Writes orders for every medication, answers pharmacist recommendations, and signs protocols such as the EpiPen protocol.

documentation: Georgia CMA Registry verification for each CMA
CMA skills competency checks, quarterly random observation reports, and annual competency reviews
Quarterly pharmacist drug regimen reviews and prescriber responses
Written orders for all medications, including OTC
Daily MARs, with 48-hour updates for new orders
Controlled substance log, updated daily, with shift-change counts
Self-administration assessments and care plan entries
EpiPen protocols and event records
Medication error and incident reports
Disposal records with two signatures

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Health and Hygiene: Infection Control, Work and Return-to-Work, Foodborne Illness, Reportable Diseases
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To protect residents, staff and visitors from preventable infection by setting rules for infection control, for when ill employees must stay out of work and when they may return, for foodborne illness prevention, and for reporting of reportable diseases.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(i) (ALC .07(2)(i) - health and hygiene issues for residents and staff relating to infection control, work policies and return to work policies, food borne illnesses and reportable diseases). Infection control: [AGENCY NAME] applies standard precautions to all residents at all times and follows the infection control and sanitation requirements of Ch. 111-8-63. Staff health: no employee provides care until the employee has had tuberculosis (TB) screening and a physical examination within the 12 months before providing care (Rule .09(10)). A resident with active TB is not admitted (Rule .15(1)). Work and return-to-work: employees with vomiting, diarrhea, fever, respiratory illness or infected skin lesions are excluded from resident care and food handling until the criteria in this policy are met. Foodborne illness: food is kept clean, wholesome and safe, and perishable food is held at or below 41 degrees F (Rule .21). Reportable diseases: the Administrator reports diseases and outbreaks that are reportable under Georgia Department of Public Health requirements to the local health district. Bloodborne pathogen exposure is managed under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030.

definitions.definition: Infection prevention practices applied to every resident regardless of diagnosis: hand hygiene, gloves and other protective equipment as needed, safe handling of sharps, cleaning of equipment and surfaces, and safe handling of linen and waste.
Removal of an ill employee from resident care, food preparation and shared work areas until return-to-work criteria are met.
Illness caused by eating contaminated food or drink, usually causing vomiting, diarrhea or fever in two or more people who ate the same food.
A disease or outbreak that Georgia Department of Public Health rules require providers to report to the local health district.
Contact of the eyes, mouth, mucous membranes, non-intact skin or a needlestick/sharps injury with blood or other potentially infectious material.

procedures: The Administrator appoints an Infection Control Coordinator [NAME/TITLE] (usually the RN or Nurse Consultant) who reviews this policy annually and keeps current guidance from the local health district.

Before an employee provides any care, the Administrator confirms that TB screening and a physical examination were completed within the preceding 12 months, and files the results in the personnel file (see STF-02).

At pre-admission screening, the Administrator or on-site manager confirms the applicant has no active TB, per Rule .15(1), through the physician's report and screening documents (see ADM-01). An applicant with signs of active TB is not admitted until medically cleared.

All staff are trained in hand hygiene, standard precautions, glove and personal protective equipment use, cleaning and disinfection, laundry handling and cough etiquette during orientation and annually. Attendance is recorded.
Alcohol-based hand rub and handwashing supplies, gloves, masks and disinfectant are kept stocked on each floor. The housekeeping supervisor checks stock weekly and restocks as needed.

An employee who has vomiting, diarrhea, fever, a respiratory illness, or an infected or weeping skin lesion must call the on-site manager before the shift. A staff member who becomes ill at work is sent home right away.

Exclusion and return-to-work criteria are: vomiting or diarrhea - out until symptom-free for at least 48 hours; fever - out until fever-free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medication; respiratory illness - out until fever-free for 24 hours and symptoms are improving, with a mask worn if cleared to return sooner by a clinician; infected skin lesions - out until lesions are covered and drainage has stopped or a clinician clears the employee; suspected or confirmed TB, or any other communicable disease - out until cleared in writing by a health care provider or the health district.

The on-site manager records each exclusion and return in the staff illness log. Staff are not penalized for staying home as this policy requires. A food handler ill with vomiting or diarrhea is not returned to food duties until the 48-hour criterion is met.

Residents with signs of infection are reported to the nurse and to the resident's physician under HLT-01. The on-site manager records symptoms, onset and actions in an infection surveillance log, which the Infection Control Coordinator reviews monthly for clusters.

Kitchen staff keep perishable food at or below 41 degrees F. They check and log refrigerator and freezer temperatures at least daily, discard food that is out of range or past its date, wash hands before handling food, and use clean, sanitized equipment (see DL-01).

When two or more residents or staff have vomiting or diarrhea in a 48-hour period, the on-site manager notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator saves any suspect food, identifies foods served and common exposures, increases cleaning, separates ill residents where possible, and calls the local health district at [LOCAL HEALTH DISTRICT PHONE].

The Administrator reports reportable diseases and outbreaks to the local health district as Georgia Department of Public Health requirements direct, and documents the date, person contacted and instructions received. The Administrator also decides whether the event is a reportable incident to DCH under ALC-09.

Following an exposure incident, the employee washes the area, reports to the on-site manager at once and is sent for medical evaluation at [OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH PROVIDER]. The Administrator completes an exposure report and keeps it in a confidential file under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030.

The Administrator keeps a written bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan, offers hepatitis B vaccination to employees with occupational exposure at no cost, supplies sharps containers and personal protective equipment, and provides training at hire and yearly.

Housekeeping cleans and disinfects high-touch surfaces daily and cleans bathrooms and shared equipment between residents. Soiled linen is bagged at the point of use and washed separately from clean linen (see DL-03).

Visitors with symptoms of contagious illness are asked to delay visits. The Administrator may restrict visits during outbreaks, informs residents and families of the reason and duration, and allows compassionate access under the community's visitation practices (see ALC-06).
The Infection Control Coordinator summarizes infections, exclusions and outbreaks quarterly for the quality assurance review (see ALC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures employee TB and physical requirements are met, decides on exclusion and return, reports reportable diseases to the health district, and reports qualifying events to DCH.
Maintains this policy, trains staff, reviews the infection log and leads outbreak response.
Enforces exclusion rules each shift, records illness reports and monitors supplies and precautions.
Controls food temperatures, food-handler health and sanitation, and saves suspect food during foodborne illness events.
Use standard precautions, stay home when ill, and report symptoms and exposures immediately.

documentation: Employee TB screening and physical examination records
Staff illness and exclusion/return-to-work log
Resident infection surveillance log
Training records for infection control and bloodborne pathogens
Refrigerator, freezer and food temperature logs
Outbreak investigation notes and health district contact records
Exposure incident reports and exposure control plan
Quarterly infection summary in the quality assurance file

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Investigation and Reporting of Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, Wandering, Accidents, Injuries and Changes in Condition
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To make sure that abuse, neglect, exploitation, wandering or missing residents, accidents, injuries and changes in condition are responded to immediately, investigated, and reported to every required party within the required time.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(j) (ALC .07(2)(j) - the investigation and reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation of residents, residents' wandering away from the community, accidents, injuries and changes in residents' conditions to required parties). Terms are used as defined in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.03. [AGENCY NAME] acts immediately on any accident or sudden adverse change in condition, notifies the resident's representative or legal surrogate, and records the change and the response in the resident file (Rule .26). The Administrator or on-site manager begins an immediate investigation into the cause of any accident, injury or death and reports the results to the representative or legal surrogate. Copies are kept in the resident file and in a central quality assurance file (Rule .26). Reports to DCH under Rule .30: the Administrator reports to DCH within 24 hours of the incident, or of reasonable cause to believe an incident occurred, any accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness; serious injury needing medical attention; rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation (Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act); external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation; and an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record. The community calls local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing (Mattie's Call Act) and reports the start and end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement.

definitions.definition: Have the meanings given in Rule .03 and the Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act. In this policy they include any willful or negligent act or omission that harms a resident, or the use of a resident's money, property or services for another person's benefit.
Harm to a resident as defined in Rule .03, which includes pressure ulcers that were not properly cared for.
An event listed for 24-hour reporting to DCH under Rule .30 (see Policy).
The statewide alert for a missing person who is elderly, disabled or cognitively impaired, activated through law enforcement when a resident is missing.
An accident or sudden or significant adverse change in a resident's physical, mental or behavioral status that requires action, notification and documentation.

procedures: Any staff member who witnesses, suspects or is told of abuse, neglect, exploitation, a fall, injury, elopement or change in condition acts at once to protect the resident, summons emergency help if needed, and tells the on-site manager immediately.

For an accident or sudden adverse change, staff give first aid or emergency care within their training, stay with the resident, and follow the emergency response steps in HLT-01. If a resident is unresponsive: if enrolled in hospice, call the hospice, then the health care agent, then EMS and start CPR unless there is a valid DNR; if there is a valid DNR, honor it in good faith; if there is a health care agent, call the agent, and if the agent cannot be reached and there is no DNR, call EMS and start CPR; if there is no hospice, DNR or directive, call EMS and start CPR unless it is clearly futile and no physician, authorized RN or PA is on site.
Staff keep emergency numbers and the resident's information readily available, and send the face sheet, medication list and directives with the resident during transport.
The on-site manager notifies the representative or legal surrogate as soon as the resident is safe, and the physician as needed. Time, person notified and response are recorded in the resident file.

For suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the on-site manager separates the resident from the alleged abuser, removes any alleged staff abuser from resident contact immediately (see ALC-10), and notifies the Administrator at once. Staff are never to investigate by questioning the resident in a way that could distress the resident or influence the account.

The Administrator or on-site manager begins an investigation immediately. This includes securing the scene and evidence, interviewing the resident, witnesses and staff separately, reviewing the care plan, staffing and records, and writing the findings and the cause. The investigation is completed within 5 business days unless a longer period is needed and documented.

The Administrator reports to DCH within 24 hours of the incident, or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred, for each event listed in the Policy section. The report states the community and Administrator names, the incident date and discovery date, the type and brief description of the incident, and the immediate corrective or preventive action taken. The Administrator keeps a copy of the transmitted report.

If a staff member, owner or director acquires a criminal record, the Administrator reports it to DCH within 24 hours of learning of it, and takes the personnel action required under ALC-10 and STF-01.

The Administrator makes the reports required by the Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act to the agencies the Act names, including the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at [OMBUDSMAN PHONE] and law enforcement when a crime may have occurred, and records each report.

When a resident is missing, staff begin an immediate search of the building and grounds. On actual knowledge that the resident is missing, the on-site manager or Administrator calls local police at [LOCAL POLICE PHONE] within 30 minutes and requests a Mattie's Call if law enforcement activates one.

The Administrator reports the start of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of contact with law enforcement, and reports its end (resident found or alert canceled) within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement. Times are recorded. The representative is notified immediately. See SAF-01 for search steps.

After a resident is found, the nurse examines the resident, the physician is notified, and the care plan and supervision level are re-evaluated within 24 hours. The wandering risk is reflected in the care plan (see ADM-02).

After any accident, injury or death, the Administrator or on-site manager records the cause, contributing factors and actions to prevent a recurrence, and reports the results of the investigation to the representative or legal surrogate.
Copies of the incident report, the investigation, notifications and DCH reports are filed in the resident file and in the central quality assurance file (see REC-01).

If DCH opens a separate complaint investigation, the Administrator cooperates fully, makes all records available to DCH inspectors, and does not retaliate against any resident, family member or employee who made or supported a report.
The Administrator reviews all incident reports each month for trends, and presents them at the quarterly quality assurance review (see ALC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Directs investigations, makes all DCH, police, ombudsman and other required reports on time, and keeps the central quality assurance file.
Responds immediately, protects the resident, notifies the representative, starts the investigation and makes the first police call for a missing resident.
Assesses the resident after an incident, advises on physician notification and reviews incident trends.
Report any suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, wandering, accident, injury or change in condition immediately and cooperate with investigations.

documentation: Incident/accident report with date, time, description and immediate action
Investigation report with interviews, evidence, cause and corrective action
Record of notification of representative or legal surrogate
DCH 24-hour reports and Mattie's Call start and end reports, with times
Police and ombudsman report records
Resident file entry of the change in condition and response
Copy in the central quality assurance file

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Discipline for Conduct Inconsistent With Community Policies
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To provide a fair, consistent and documented process for correcting or ending the employment of staff whose conduct is inconsistent with community policies, and to protect residents from harm while concerns are reviewed.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(k) (ALC .07(2)(k) - discipline procedures for handling acts committed by staff which are inconsistent with the policies of the assisted living community). [AGENCY NAME] disciplines any staff member whose conduct is inconsistent with community policies, state rules or resident rights. A staff member may not be impaired while on duty (Rule .09(17)). A staff member may not coerce, pressure or influence a resident to assign money, valuables or property to the community or any person (Rule .25). Staff are removed from resident contact pending an investigation of any allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation. An employee who acquires a criminal record is reported to DCH within 24 hours (Rule .30). Discipline is progressive except where the conduct is serious enough to warrant immediate action. All discipline is documented and kept in the personnel file, which is retained for 3 years after the employee leaves (Rule .09). No resident, family member or employee is punished or harassed for reporting a concern or enforcing a resident's rights (Rule .25).

definitions.definition: Any act or omission that violates a community policy, house rule, state regulation, resident right or professional standard, including abuse, neglect, exploitation, impairment on duty, falsifying records, coercion for money or property, and unsafe care.
A sequence of documented steps - verbal counseling, written warning, final written warning, termination - applied in proportion to the seriousness and history of the conduct.
Immediate removal from resident contact or from the schedule, with or without pay as policy provides, while an allegation is investigated.
A condition in which an employee's ability to perform safely is reduced by alcohol, drugs, medication, illness or another cause.

procedures: At hire and annually, each employee receives and signs the code of conduct and this policy. The signed copy is kept in the personnel file (see STF-02).

Any staff member who becomes aware of conduct inconsistent with policy reports it to the on-site manager or Administrator at once. If the concern involves the Administrator, the report goes to [OWNER/GOVERNING BODY CONTACT]. Reports can be made in confidence, and retaliation is prohibited.
The supervisor or Administrator documents the facts on an incident or disciplinary form on the day they become known: who, what, when, where and witnesses, in neutral language.

If the conduct could involve abuse, neglect or exploitation of a resident, the Administrator removes the employee from all resident contact immediately, and the investigation and reports proceed under ALC-09. Return to duty requires the Administrator's written decision after the investigation.

The Administrator investigates promptly by reviewing records and interviewing the employee, witnesses and, if appropriate, the resident. The employee is given an opportunity to respond, and the response is recorded.

Suspected impairment: the supervisor who observes signs (for example odor of alcohol, unsteadiness, slurred speech, unusual behavior) takes the employee aside with a second manager as witness, documents the observations, and removes the employee from resident care. The employee is not allowed to drive, and the supervisor arranges safe transportation home. Testing and next steps follow community drug and alcohol procedures [DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE POLICY REFERENCE]. Confirmed impairment on duty is a ground for termination.

Suspected coercion or exploitation: any report that a staff member asked for, accepted or arranged the assignment of money, valuables or property from a resident is treated as suspected exploitation. The employee is removed from resident contact, the resident's property is secured and documented under RR-03, and reports are made under ALC-09.

Progressive steps for lesser violations are: (1) verbal counseling, documented; (2) written warning; (3) final written warning, possibly with suspension; (4) termination. The Administrator may begin at any step based on the seriousness of the conduct.

The following warrant immediate termination after investigation: abuse, neglect or exploitation of a resident; theft; coercing a resident to assign money, valuables or property; working while impaired; falsifying medication, care or time records; and any conduct that places a resident in immediate danger.

The Administrator meets with the employee, explains the finding and the action, and gives a copy of the disciplinary notice. The employee signs to acknowledge receipt, or the Administrator notes a refusal to sign.

If an employee, owner or director acquires a criminal record, the Administrator reports it to DCH within 24 hours of learning of it, reviews the matter with the background check requirements in STF-01, and decides whether the employee may continue working.
The Administrator makes any other report required by law, such as a report to the appropriate licensing board or registry about a CMA or other certified staff member, and records it.
Retraining or corrective action required by the discipline (for example medication retraining under ALC-07) is scheduled with a date, completed, and recorded.
The disciplinary file is placed in the personnel file and kept for 3 years after the employee leaves. Disciplinary information is shared only with those who need it.
The Administrator reviews discipline trends at the quarterly quality assurance review without identifying residents, and updates training where patterns appear (see ALC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Decides on discipline, removal and termination, makes DCH and other reports, and keeps discipline records.
Document concerns, apply administrative removal when safety requires it and deliver counseling.
Reviews any concern involving the Administrator and supports consistent enforcement.
Follow policy, report violations and cooperate with investigations.

documentation: Signed code of conduct acknowledgment
Incident and disciplinary forms with employee responses
Administrative removal and return-to-duty decisions
Impairment observation record
Investigation file for any abuse, neglect or exploitation allegation
DCH report of employee criminal record, with date and time
Personnel file retained 3 years after the employee leaves

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Drills and Evacuation
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To make sure the community is ready to protect residents in a fire, severe weather, power or water loss, medical emergency or other disaster, and that staff and residents know what to do and how to evacuate or relocate safely.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(l) (ALC .07(2)(l) - emergency preparedness, drills and evacuation requirements). [AGENCY NAME] complies with Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans) as Rule .14 requires. The written disaster plan is readily accessible to staff, residents and families, and names the staff positions responsible for implementing the plan and for obtaining emergency medical attention. Evacuation maps with marked escape routes are posted on each floor. A clear, accessible emergency route through common areas is kept at all times. If an emergency forces relocation, the Administrator gives timely notice of the new address to residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH. The interior and exterior of the community are kept in good repair and free of unsafe conditions, and entrances, exits, sidewalks and escape routes are kept free of hazards (Rule .13). The community keeps the current State Fire Marshal report showing no violations and the approved capacity load, and the electrician compliance documentation required for licensure. Fire drills are held and recorded as the State Fire Marshal and Rule .13 require.

definitions.definition: The written plan required by Ch. 111-8-16 that covers fire, severe weather, utility failure, medical emergencies, evacuation and relocation.
A posted floor plan showing the viewer's location, marked escape routes, exits and assembly points.
The temporary or permanent move of residents to another location because an emergency makes the community unsafe to occupy.
The maximum number of residents the State Fire Marshal report approves for the building.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written disaster plan that complies with Ch. 111-8-16, covering fire, tornado and severe weather, flood, power and water loss, loss of heat or air conditioning, bomb threat, infectious disease outbreak, utility failure, missing resident and loss of staff.

The plan names the staff positions responsible for carrying it out and for obtaining emergency medical attention, with a named alternate for each position on every shift. The plan lists emergency numbers for 911, fire, police, poison control, the local emergency management agency, utilities, hospital, pharmacy, DCH at [DCH CONTACT], and the representatives of each resident.

The plan is kept in a binder at [LOCATION], where staff, residents and families can easily get it. The Administrator tells residents and families where it is during admission and at resident and family meetings.
The Administrator posts evacuation maps with marked escape routes on each floor, checks them monthly, and updates them after any change in floor plan or room use.

The maintenance supervisor checks every day that entrances, exits, sidewalks, stairs, hallways and escape routes are clear of hazards, and that a clear, accessible emergency route through common areas is kept open. Hazards are removed immediately and the check is recorded.

At least two direct care staff, with at least one on each occupied floor, are on duty at all times. The staffing plan identifies who assists residents who cannot self-evacuate and which staff close doors, account for residents and call 911 (see ALC-02).

Fire drills are held and recorded as the State Fire Marshal and Rule .13 require. As a minimum internal standard, [AGENCY NAME] holds a drill at least quarterly on each shift, varies the time and conditions, and holds more often if the Fire Marshal or Ch. 111-8-16 requires. Each drill record includes date, time, shift, evacuation time, participants, problems found and corrective action.
Severe weather and other emergency drills in the plan are practiced at least annually, and shelter-in-place and relocation steps are walked through with staff.

Each resident's care plan documents mobility and assisted-self-preservation needs, and the on-site manager keeps a current list of residents who need help to evacuate, for use in an emergency (see ADM-02).

The Administrator keeps current the State Fire Marshal report showing no violations and the capacity load, and the electrician compliance form. The Administrator orders new inspections before the application time limits expire or when DCH or the Fire Marshal requires, and corrects any violation by the date given.

Smoke detection, alarms, extinguishers and emergency lighting are tested and inspected on the schedule the Fire Marshal requires, with test records kept (see SAF-03). The maintenance supervisor reports defects to the Administrator the same day.
New staff are trained in the disaster plan, alarm systems, extinguisher use and evacuation routes during orientation, and all staff are retrained annually (see ALC-04).

In an emergency, the responsible staff position calls 911 first, begins the response in the plan, accounts for all residents against the census and takes medications, records and the resident face sheets with them if evacuating.

If an emergency forces relocation, the Administrator or designee notifies residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH promptly of the relocation address, and keeps a record of each notification and the time. Residents' care, medications and records are moved with them.

After any emergency or drill, the Administrator holds a debrief within 7 days, records lessons learned and updates the plan. A disaster or emergency that affects safe operation of the community is reported under ALC-09.
The Administrator reviews the plan at least annually and after any actual emergency, and the review is included in the quality assurance report (see ALC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains and updates the disaster plan, schedules drills, keeps Fire Marshal and electrician documents current, and notifies residents, families, representatives and DCH of any relocation.
Directs the response on the shift, accounts for residents and obtains emergency medical attention.
Keeps escape routes clear and the building safe, and tests alarms and equipment.
Know their role and evacuation routes, take part in drills and assist residents.

documentation: Written disaster plan, with staff positions named
Posted evacuation maps (floor-by-floor check log)
Fire and emergency drill records
State Fire Marshal report (no violations, capacity load) and electrician compliance form
Daily hazard and escape route check records
List of residents needing evacuation assistance
Relocation notification record
Post-emergency debrief records and plan updates

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Quality Assurance Review and Resident/Family Feedback
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To create a regular review process that uses incident data, inspection findings and resident and family feedback to find and carry out improvements in care and services.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(m) (ALC .07(2)(m) - quality assurance review mechanisms, including resident and family feedback to determine opportunities for improving care). [AGENCY NAME] keeps a central quality assurance file that holds the investigations of accidents, injuries and deaths required by Rule .26. The quality assurance committee reviews incident trends, inspection findings and plans of correction on a quarterly schedule. The community obtains resident and family feedback through surveys, resident council meetings and an open-door practice, records each concern and the action taken, and does not punish or harass anyone for giving feedback or enforcing rights (Rule .25). Inspection report disputes and the written plan of correction are due within 10 days of receipt of the report, and the plan states date-certain actions (Rule .10). The most recent inspection report and plan of correction are displayed where residents and visitors can see them, and the community keeps an accurate licensed residential care profile (Rule .10).

definitions.definition: The central file of incident and accident investigations, QA committee minutes, survey results, corrective actions and inspection documents.
The written response to an inspection report listing the actions to be taken to correct each deficiency and the date each will be complete.
The profile of the community kept accurate with DCH, which must match the license, the services provided and the community's marketing.
Any comment, suggestion, concern or complaint from a resident, family member, representative or visitor about care or services. Formal grievances follow RR-01.

procedures: The Administrator names a QA committee made up of the Administrator, the RN or Nurse Consultant, the dietary and housekeeping supervisors, a direct care staff member and, when willing, a resident or family representative. The committee meets at least quarterly and records minutes.

The central QA file is kept by the Administrator. It holds copies of each investigation of an accident, injury or death, the report to the representative or legal surrogate, serious incident reports, and the QA committee minutes (see ALC-09).

Before each meeting, the nurse compiles data on falls, injuries, elopements and wandering, medication errors, infections, skin integrity, hospital transfers, deaths, staff turnover and grievances, without naming residents in the summary.

At each meeting, the committee reviews trends, compares results to the prior quarter, identifies root causes, decides on corrective actions with an owner and due date, and checks whether earlier actions worked. The decisions are recorded in the minutes.
The committee reviews each DCH inspection report and plan of correction, and any complaint finding, to check that corrections are carried out and kept in place.

Residents and families are asked for feedback at admission, at each care plan review, at the resident council, through an annual written survey and through a suggestion box at [LOCATION]. Anonymous feedback is accepted, and help is given to residents who need assistance to give it.

The Administrator holds a resident council meeting at least quarterly [or at the frequency set in house rules] and a family meeting at least [TWICE] a year. Meetings are announced in advance and minutes record concerns and the responses.

Staff acknowledge each concern within 1 business day, and the Administrator responds in writing or in person within [7] days, telling the person what was done. The concern and action are recorded in the feedback log. A formal grievance goes to RR-01.

The community states in house rules, at admission and by posted notice that residents and families may give feedback and make complaints without fear of punishment or harassment. The State Long-Term Care Ombudsman's contact details are posted in a common area (see RR-01 and ALC-06).

The Administrator reviews survey results and feedback logs with the QA committee and identifies opportunities to improve care. Resulting changes in staffing, training, menus, activities, care practices or policies are recorded, and residents and families are told what changed and why.

On receiving a DCH inspection report, the Administrator logs the date received. If the community disputes a finding, the written dispute is sent within 10 days of receipt. The written plan of correction, with date-certain actions for each deficiency, is submitted to DCH within 10 days of receipt.

The Administrator displays the most recent inspection report and plan of correction where residents and visitors can see them. If the community has a website, the Administrator keeps a link to the previous 18 months of inspection reports and plans of correction.

The Administrator checks the licensed residential care profile at least quarterly and after any change in services, capacity or ownership, and corrects it with DCH. The Administrator checks that services advertised and marketing materials match the license, the profile and the rules, and that no memory care is offered without a current memory care certificate.
The Administrator reports the QA summary and corrective actions to the governing body at least quarterly, and the governing body documents its review (see GOV-02).
QA records are kept available for DCH inspectors, who may inspect without notice.

responsibilities.duty: Leads the QA program, keeps the QA file, responds to inspection reports within 10 days and reports to the governing body.
Reviews data, feedback and inspection findings, and assigns and follows up on corrective actions.
Compiles clinical and incident trend data and recommends clinical improvements.
Reviews QA reports at least quarterly and supports needed changes.
Record and pass on feedback and take part in corrective actions.

documentation: Central QA file with accident, injury and death investigations
QA committee membership, agendas and quarterly minutes
Incident trend summaries
Resident and family surveys, resident council and family meeting minutes
Feedback log with responses and actions taken
DCH inspection reports, disputes and plans of correction with dates of receipt and submission
Posted inspection report and plan of correction, and website link check (if the community has a website)
Licensed residential care profile review record
Governing body review record

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Use of Volunteers and Proxy Caregivers
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] uses volunteers and permits designated proxy caregivers. Volunteers must be oriented on resident rights and basic safety precautions before they have contact with residents. Proxy caregivers must be overseen in the way Georgia law, Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63 and Chapter 111-8-100 require. Neither group may be used to meet staffing requirements or to replace trained staff.
policies.policy:
This policy meets ALC .07(2)(n) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(n)) — the use of volunteers and their orientation regarding resident's rights and basic safety precautions. It also meets ALC .07(2)(o) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(o)) — the specific use of proxy caregivers allowed within the community and the oversight of proxy caregivers the community requires or provides, in accordance with Georgia law, Chapter 111-8-63 and the proxy caregiver rules, Chapter 111-8-100.

VOLUNTEERS. [AGENCY NAME] welcomes volunteers for social, spiritual, recreational and companionship activities. No volunteer may have contact with a resident until the volunteer has received and signed for an orientation on resident rights (ALC-06) and basic safety precautions. Volunteers are never counted toward the staffing minimums or ratios in ALC-02 and Rule .09, and they never replace the required on-site direct care staff. Volunteers do not perform hands-on personal care, transfers, toileting, bathing or any medication task. Only certified medication aides (CMAs) may administer medications for the community under Rule .09(8). Volunteers are supervised by a designated staff member and are not left alone with a resident. A volunteer under 18 is under line-of-sight supervision of a staff member at all times, consistent with the standard that applies to staff under Rule .09(1).

PROXY CAREGIVERS. [AGENCY NAME] permits proxy caregivers. A proxy caregiver is an individual who is not an employee of the community and who is designated in writing by the resident or the resident's representative or legal surrogate to provide certain care for that resident, as defined in Rule .03 and Chapter 111-8-100. The community allows proxy caregivers only for the tasks and under the conditions Chapter 111-8-100 permits, and only after the community has verified the training Chapter 111-8-100 requires. The options for proxy caregiver arrangements are described in ALC-01. A proxy caregiver acts for the resident and is not community staff. Proxy caregivers are not counted toward staffing. They do not administer medications on behalf of the community, and CMAs remain the only persons who administer medications for the community. The community keeps a roster of designated proxy caregivers and oversees them as set out in the procedures below, because proxy caregivers also fall within the safety precautions in ALC-14.

definitions.definition: A person who freely offers unpaid time to the community, is not an employee, and is not a proxy caregiver for a specific resident.

An individual not employed by the community who is designated in writing by a resident or the resident's representative or legal surrogate to provide specified care to that resident, as defined in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.03 and governed by Chapter 111-8-100.
A documented session given before first resident contact covering resident rights, basic safety precautions, confidentiality and limits on volunteer activities.
A current list kept by the administrator of every designated proxy caregiver, the resident served, the tasks designated, training verification and review dates.
A certified medication aide, the only category of community staff who may administer medications under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09(8).

procedures: The Activities Director (or designee) screens each volunteer applicant. The administrator checks the National Sex Offender Registry for any volunteer who will have regular contact with residents and applies STF-01 where it applies. The administrator approves each volunteer in writing before first contact.

Before any contact with residents, the administrator or designee gives each approved volunteer a volunteer orientation covering: resident rights (ALC-06); privacy and confidentiality (RR-05); recognizing and immediately reporting suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation (ALC-09); fire, evacuation and emergency procedures (ALC-11); hand hygiene and illness exclusion (ALC-08); elopement awareness (SAF-01); and who to ask for help.

The volunteer signs the Volunteer Orientation Acknowledgment, which also states the limits on volunteer activities. The administrator keeps the signed form in the volunteer file and enters the volunteer in the Volunteer Log.

The administrator issues a visible volunteer badge. The volunteer signs in and out at the front desk on each visit. A volunteer with fever, vomiting, diarrhea, a rash or other signs of contagious illness does not enter the community until cleared under ALC-08.

The supervising staff member assigns volunteer tasks that are limited to companionship, activities, reading, social events, clerical help and similar non-care tasks. Volunteers do not perform transfers, toileting, bathing, medication tasks or any hands-on care, and they do not count toward staffing minimums.

Each shift, the shift supervisor confirms the required on-site direct care staff, with at least two staff and one per occupied floor, without counting any volunteer. The supervisor documents this on the staffing schedule.
A volunteer who observes or suspects abuse, neglect, exploitation or an injury reports it immediately to the shift supervisor and administrator. The administrator follows ALC-09.

At least once a year, the administrator reviews the Volunteer Log and re-orients volunteers who remain active. The administrator ends a volunteer's service for any breach of resident rights, confidentiality or the limits on activities.

A resident or the resident's representative or legal surrogate who wants a proxy caregiver submits a written designation naming the proxy, the resident and the tasks designated. The administrator or on-site manager reviews it with the resident or representative and records it in the resident's record and care plan (ADM-02).

Before the proxy performs any task, the administrator or on-site manager verifies and copies the proxy's completed training required by Chapter 111-8-100, checks the National Sex Offender Registry, checks photo identification, and gives the proxy an orientation on the community's emergency, infection control, reporting and resident rights procedures.

The administrator enters the proxy on the Proxy Caregiver Roster (name, resident, contact information, tasks designated, training verified, date of last review). The roster is kept current and available to DCH surveyors on request.

The proxy signs in and out on each visit and wears a visitor/proxy badge. The administrator or nurse reviews the proxy's role with the resident or representative at least every 90 days and whenever the resident's condition changes substantially (HLT-01), and updates the roster and care plan.

Proxy caregivers do not administer medications on behalf of the community and do not take the place of community staff. The community's medication administration remains with CMAs under ALC-07. The nurse reviews any task the proxy performs that touches the resident's medications or treatments with the resident's physician or professional as ALC-07 requires.

If the administrator or nurse has a concern about a proxy's competence or conduct, the administrator meets with the proxy and the resident or representative, retrains or restricts the proxy's tasks, or ends the arrangement, and documents the action. The community ensures resident care continues through community staff.

Any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation involving a volunteer or proxy caregiver is reported and investigated under ALC-09, and the individual's access is suspended at once while the investigation is pending. Safety precautions for proxies and other outside individuals are applied under ALC-14.
The QA committee reviews volunteer and proxy caregiver incidents and complaints quarterly under ALC-12.

responsibilities.duty: Approves volunteers; keeps the Volunteer Log and Proxy Caregiver Roster; verifies proxy training; suspends or ends access; ensures volunteers and proxies are never counted toward staffing.
Recruits and schedules volunteers, assigns appropriate tasks and ensures supervision.
Supervises volunteers during activities, confirms the staffing minimum is met by staff alone, and reports concerns at once.
Reviews proxy caregiver tasks affecting care and medications with the resident's physician or professional, and participates in 90-day reviews.
Remain the only community staff who administer medications.
Follow the orientation, stay within permitted tasks, sign in and out, protect confidentiality and report concerns.

documentation: Volunteer application and approval, and registry inquiry result
Signed Volunteer Orientation Acknowledgment
Volunteer Log and visitor sign-in records
Written proxy caregiver designation by the resident or representative
Copy of proxy caregiver training under Chapter 111-8-100
Proxy Caregiver Roster
90-day proxy review notes and care plan entries
Incident, complaint and corrective action records involving volunteers or proxies

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Safety and Security Precautions Against Harm by Other Residents, Proxy Caregivers and Outside Individuals
policies.applies_to: ALC
policies.purpose: To describe the safety and security precautions [AGENCY NAME] uses to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers, and other individuals who are not employed by the community but routinely come into it, such as hospice, home health, vendors and contractors, while preserving residents' rights to privacy and free communication.
policies.policy:
This policy meets ALC .07(2)(p) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07(2)(p)) — the safety and security precautions employed by the community to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers and other individuals, not employed by the community, who routinely come into the community.

Before admission, the administrator or on-site manager documents a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check for every applicant (Rule .15(2)) and documents the added safety measures [AGENCY NAME] will use for any applicant who is a registered sex offender or violent offender. Outside individuals sign in, wear identification and are screened according to their role. Staff wear ID badges (Rule .09(22)). The community keeps at least two direct care staff on site at all times, with one per occupied floor (Rule .09), so that residents are observed and help is available. Safety precautions never override resident rights under Rule .25. Residents keep private communication and privacy in their rooms, and staff knock before entering. Restraints, isolation and confinement are not used as safety measures (see SAF-02). When one resident harms or threatens another, staff follow the resident-to-resident incident protocol: separate, assess, notify, report and revise the care plan.

definitions.definition: Any person not employed by the community who routinely enters it, including hospice and home health staff, vendors, contractors, volunteers, visitors and designated proxy caregivers.

definitions.term: Registered sex offender or violent offender
definitions.definition: A person identified through a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry, a fingerprint check or other information obtained before admission as a registered sex offender or as having a history of violent offenses.
Documented, individualized precautions, such as room placement, supervision level and visitor controls, used to protect other residents without violating the offending resident's rights.
Any physical, verbal, sexual or other aggressive act or threat by one resident toward another.
An individual not employed by the community, designated in writing to provide specific care for a resident under Chapter 111-8-100 (see ALC-13).

procedures: Before an applicant is admitted, the administrator or on-site manager performs and documents a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and records the date, the person who performed it and the result on the Admission Safety Screening form (ADM-01).

If the applicant is a registered sex offender or has a violent offense history, the administrator, the nurse and the on-site manager meet before the admission decision and document the added safety measures. These may include a room away from residents who are cognitively impaired or vulnerable, increased supervision in common areas, no unsupervised entry into other residents' rooms, a staff briefing on the care plan, and visitor controls.

The administrator tells the resident or representative, in writing, of the added safety measures that apply to the resident. The measures are entered in the care plan (ADM-02) and reviewed at least quarterly and after any incident. If the community cannot keep other residents safe, the administrator declines the admission under ADM-01.

The front desk staff require every visitor to sign in and out with name, date, time and resident visited. Visitors are escorted or redirected if they are not known to staff, and visiting follows the house rules (ALC-05).

Vendors, contractors and delivery personnel sign in, show identification, state their purpose, wear a visitor badge and are escorted or directed to the work area. Contractors do not enter resident rooms without staff knowledge and the resident's permission.

Before a hospice, home health or other outside provider begins service, the administrator verifies the agency name, the staff member's photo ID and the care arrangement with the resident or representative. These providers sign in at each visit and wear agency identification. Staff coordinate with them under HLT-04.

Designated proxy caregivers are verified, trained and listed on the roster as set out in ALC-13. They sign in at each visit and wear a visitor/proxy badge. The administrator suspends a proxy's access at once if there is a safety concern.
All community employees wear an ID badge with name and title while on duty (Rule .09(22)). Staff challenge, politely, any person without a badge and notify the shift supervisor.

The shift supervisor secures exterior doors and monitors entrances according to the building security plan and SAF-01. The community never locks a resident into or out of the resident's bedroom, and common area access is not restricted as a security measure.

Residents keep private communication and privacy in their rooms. Staff knock before entering, and residents' mail, phone calls and visits are not censored or monitored as a security measure (Rule .25). Searches of rooms or belongings are not conducted unless the resident consents or an emergency requires it.

Staff observe and record behaviors that may signal risk to others, such as aggression, threats, unwanted sexual advances or wandering into other residents' rooms. They report them to the shift supervisor and nurse the same shift and document them in the resident's record.

RESIDENT-TO-RESIDENT INCIDENT PROTOCOL. SEPARATE: staff immediately and calmly separate the residents and make sure both are safe. ASSESS: a nurse or the shift supervisor checks both residents for injury, calls 911 for emergencies and documents findings.

NOTIFY: the shift supervisor notifies the administrator at once and notifies the representatives or legal surrogates of both residents and each resident's physician as soon as possible and the same shift. REPORT: the administrator investigates and reports under ALC-09 and REC-02, including to law enforcement or DCH when required.

REVISE: within 72 hours the nurse and administrator revise the care plan of each resident involved, which may include room changes, increased supervision, behavior interventions, physician review or reassessment of whether the community can continue to meet the aggressive resident's needs (ADM-03).

If an outside individual or visitor threatens or harms a resident, staff keep the resident safe, call 911 if there is danger, ask the individual to leave, and notify the administrator. The administrator may restrict the individual's visits only as the resident's rights allow, and with the resident's input, and reports the event under ALC-09.

The administrator reviews all safety and security incidents, registry-related measures and visitor concerns at the quarterly QA meeting (ALC-12). Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually under ALC-04.

responsibilities.duty: Completes and documents registry or fingerprint checks; decides on admission and added safety measures; investigates and reports incidents; restricts access when needed.
Assesses residents after incidents, helps develop added safety measures and updates care plans.
Directs the incident protocol, secures entrances, enforces sign-in and badges and notifies the administrator.
Wear ID badges, observe residents, report behaviors, and separate residents safely.
Maintain the visitor and vendor sign-in logs and issue badges.

documentation: Admission Safety Screening form with National Sex Offender Registry or fingerprint results
Documentation of added safety measures and resident/representative notice
Visitor, vendor, contractor and outside provider sign-in logs
Proxy Caregiver Roster (see ALC-13)
Resident-to-resident incident reports and investigation notes
Notification records to representatives, physicians, law enforcement and DCH
Revised care plans after incidents
QA meeting minutes on safety and security

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Services Available in the Home (Personal Services, Memory Care, Proxy Caregivers)
policies.applies_to: PCH
policies.purpose: To state clearly which services [AGENCY NAME], a licensed personal care home, provides, which it does not provide, and how those services match the permit DCH has issued, so that residents, families, staff and surveyors have the same understanding.
policies.policy:
This policy meets PCH .07(3)(a) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07(3)(a)) — the services available in the home, including personal services, memory care services/centers and any other specialized services such as designated proxy caregivers.

PERSONAL SERVICES. [AGENCY NAME] provides personal services and supervision to residents who meet the admission criteria in PCH-02: assistance with activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, eating, mobility and transfers), protective care and watchful oversight, three meals a day with snacks and therapeutic diets as ordered (DL-01), laundry and housekeeping (DL-03), help with self-administered medications as the home's medication policy allows (PCH-06), daily social and leisure activities and transportation (DL-02), and an operable, non-pay telephone available for staff emergency use and for private resident access. Following the standard in the comparable assisted living rule (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.17), each resident receives a needs assessment and a written care plan within 14 days of admission, updated at least annually and whenever needs change substantially. The home does not restrict free access to common areas and does not lock a resident into or out of the resident's bedroom.

SERVICES NOT PROVIDED. A personal care home may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an assisted living community (ALC) license (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62). [AGENCY NAME] does not provide assisted living care and does not advertise or market it. Periodic or short-term medical and nursing services are not provided as home services. They may be purchased by the resident from a licensed provider, such as a home health agency, with the exception of care planning, training, medication administration and competency checks that the home performs under its own policies (see HLT-04).

MEMORY CARE. No memory care center may operate without a current DCH certificate (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.05); the certificate fee is $200 per year. [AGENCY NAME] provides memory care services only in a unit or area covered by a current certificate, and the dementia training required by PCH-03 and HLT-02 is in place before any resident is placed there. Without a current certificate, the home does not hold itself out as a memory care provider.

PROXY CAREGIVERS. Designated proxy caregivers may provide care to a specific resident only under Chapter 111-8-100 and the home's oversight requirements in PCH-12.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PERMIT. Services described in the admission agreement, brochures, website and verbal marketing must match the services this policy lists and the home's DCH permit (see GOV-01). The administrator reviews this policy against the current text of Chapter 111-8-62 at each annual policy review and whenever the rule changes.

definitions.definition: Assistance with activities of daily living and the protective care, supervision and meals, laundry and housekeeping the home furnishes to residents who meet its admission criteria.
A level of care that a personal care home may not provide unless it holds an ALC license.
A unit or home that provides care for residents with dementia and requires a current DCH certificate before it may operate.
An individual not employed by the home who is designated in writing to give specified care to a particular resident under Chapter 111-8-100.
The current DCH permit authorizing the home to operate as a personal care home at its licensed capacity.

procedures: The administrator maintains the Services Available list in this policy and reviews it at least annually and before any change in services. Any change is made only after confirming it is consistent with the home's DCH permit and Chapter 111-8-62.

The administrator makes sure the admission agreement (RR-02) describes the services provided, the services not provided and the fee for each service, and gives a copy of the Services Available list to every applicant before admission.

During pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the administrator or on-site manager compares the applicant's needs to the services on the list. If the applicant needs services the home does not provide, the administrator declines the admission and offers referral information.

Within 14 days of admission, the administrator or on-site manager (with the nurse if available) completes the resident needs assessment covering family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral status and preferences, and writes the care plan (ADM-02). The care plan is updated at least annually and whenever the resident's needs change substantially.
Direct care staff provide the personal services in each care plan, and document them on the daily service record each shift. The supervisor reviews the records weekly.
The home provides at least one planned social or leisure activity every day, posted on the activity calendar, and staff record each resident's participation (DL-02).
The administrator ensures a working, non-pay telephone is available for staff use in an emergency and that residents can use a telephone privately.

When a resident needs periodic or short-term nursing or medical services, the administrator helps the resident or representative arrange them with a licensed provider of the resident's choice, and records the arrangement in the care plan (HLT-04).

If the home wants to offer memory care, the administrator first applies to DCH for the memory care certificate, pays the $200 annual fee and does not admit or place any resident in memory care until the certificate is issued and posted (GOV-01, HLT-02).
Staff direct any request for assisted living-level care, such as continuous nursing care, to the administrator, who evaluates under PCH-02 whether the resident may be retained or must be transferred.
When a resident or representative designates a proxy caregiver, the administrator follows PCH-12 to verify training, maintain the roster and oversee the proxy.

Before any brochure, website or advertisement is published, the administrator reviews it to confirm that it describes only the services this policy lists and the permit allows. Marketing materials are kept on file with the review date.
The administrator reviews this policy against the current text of Chapter 111-8-62 each year and documents the review in the policy review log (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the Services Available list; ensures services and marketing match the permit; obtains the memory care certificate before offering memory care; reviews this policy annually.
Completes needs assessments and care plans within 14 days and confirms daily services are delivered.
Provide personal services per the care plan and document each shift.
Provide daily social activities and record participation.
Assists with assessments, care plans and arrangement of outside nursing services.

documentation: Services Available list and annual review log
Admission agreement with services and fees (RR-02)
Resident needs assessment and care plan (completed within 14 days)
Daily service records and activity calendars with participation logs
Current DCH permit and, if applicable, memory care certificate and $200 fee receipt
Reviewed brochures and marketing materials
Proxy caregiver roster (PCH-12)

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Admissions, Discharges, Immediate Transfers and Refunds
policies.applies_to: PCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] admits and keeps only residents whose needs it is authorized and able to meet, handles discharges and immediate transfers safely and with proper notice, and refunds money owed to residents or their estates when a resident is transferred or discharged.
policies.policy:
This policy meets PCH .07(3)(b) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07(3)(b)) — admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the home does not admit or retain residents who need more care than the home is authorized or capable of providing. It also meets PCH .07(3)(c) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07(3)(c)) — refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged.

ADMISSION AND RETENTION. The home does not admit or retain a resident who needs more care than the home is authorized by its DCH permit, or is able, to provide. Using the model in the assisted living admission rule (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.15) as its standard, and subject to confirmation against Chapter 111-8-62, the home admits only persons who are 18 or older, do not have active tuberculosis, do not need continuous medical or nursing care, do not need physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control, can actively participate in transfers and can participate in social and leisure activities. Before admission, the administrator or on-site manager documents the evaluation of the applicant, including a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and added safety measures if needed (PCH-13), and obtains the physician evaluation on the required DCH form.

DISCHARGE AND TRANSFER. Each admission agreement contains a written procedure for discharge and transfer. The administrator or on-site manager contacts the resident's representative or legal surrogate when discharge or transfer becomes necessary. The home gives 30 days' written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required (see Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.29, followed as the home's standard). An immediate transfer is used only when the resident's condition or behavior creates an urgent medical need or an immediate danger to the resident or others.

REFUNDS. When a resident dies, is transferred or is discharged, the home refunds all prepaid amounts for days the resident did not occupy the bed and any deposit owed, as the admission agreement (which must include a refund policy) states. The home pays the refund to the resident, the representative or the estate no later than 30 days after the resident's departure or death, or sooner if the admission agreement or applicable law requires.

CHANGE OF OWNERSHIP OR CLOSURE. The home gives at least 30 days' written notice to DCH and to residents of a change of ownership or closure, and 60 days' notice for impending bankruptcy or eviction (see GOV-01).

definitions.definition: A transfer made without the standard 30-day notice because the resident needs urgent medical care or poses an immediate danger to self or others.
Care and services allowed by the home's DCH permit and Chapter 111-8-62.
Care the home's staffing, training, physical plant and policies can safely deliver to a particular resident.
A person authorized by the resident or the law to act for the resident (see RR-04).
Return of prepaid fees, deposits and any resident funds owed upon death, transfer or discharge.

procedures: The administrator or on-site manager completes pre-admission screening (ADM-01) with every applicant. It includes an interview, a review of the physician evaluation on the DCH form, a review of medications and behaviors, and a comparison of the applicant's needs to PCH-01 and the permit.

The administrator or on-site manager checks the applicant against the admission criteria: age 18 or older; no active TB; no need for continuous medical or nursing care; no need for restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control; ability to take part in transfers; and ability to take part in social and leisure activities. The result is documented on the Admission Evaluation form.

Before admission, the administrator or on-site manager documents the National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and any added safety measures for a registered sex offender or violent offender (PCH-13).

The administrator makes the admission decision in writing the same day the evaluation is complete. If the home cannot meet the applicant's needs, the administrator declines and gives the applicant or representative written reasons and referral options.

The administrator reviews the plain-language admission agreement (RR-02) with the resident or representative before signing. The agreement states fees, discharge and transfer procedures, the complaint process, transportation and the refund policy. The resident or representative receives a signed copy.

Staff reassess each resident whenever a change in condition occurs and at least annually (ADM-02). If a resident's needs appear to exceed what the home is authorized or able to provide, the administrator consults the resident, representative and physician within 48 hours to decide on added services, outside services or transfer.

When discharge or transfer is needed, the administrator or on-site manager contacts the resident's representative or legal surrogate promptly, and in all cases before written notice is delivered, and helps plan the move (ADM-03).

The administrator gives the resident and representative written notice at least 30 days before a planned discharge or transfer, stating the reason, the effective date and the resident's right to use the complaint process (RR-01) and to contact the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman.

For an immediate transfer, staff call 911 or arrange emergency transport as the situation requires. The shift supervisor immediately notifies the administrator, the representative or surrogate and the physician, sends current medications, the face sheet and medication record with the resident, and documents the event (HLT-01).

Within 24 hours after an immediate transfer, the administrator delivers written notice of the reason for the transfer to the resident or representative. If the resident cannot return, the administrator follows the discharge steps and the refund steps in this policy.

On the day of discharge, transfer or death, the administrator or on-site manager returns the resident's personal property and funds under RR-03, records an inventory signed by the receiving party, and sends a copy of the discharge summary and medication list to the receiving provider.

The administrator calculates any refund on the Resident Account Reconciliation form within 7 days: prepaid fees minus the daily charges through the date the bed is vacated (the date of death or removal of belongings, whichever is later, as the admission agreement states), plus any deposit owed. A second person reviews the calculation.

The administrator pays the refund to the resident, representative or estate within 30 days of the departure or death, keeps a copy of the check or transfer record, and sends an itemized statement with it.

The administrator notifies DCH in writing at least 30 days before any change of ownership or closure, and at least 60 days before for impending bankruptcy or eviction, and gives each resident and representative the same written notice and relocation help (GOV-01, ADM-03).

The administrator reviews all discharges, transfers and refunds quarterly through the QA process (PCH-11), looking for patterns, such as repeated admissions of residents whose needs exceed what the home provides.

responsibilities.duty: Makes admission, retention and discharge decisions; ensures notices and refunds are timely and accurate; notifies DCH of ownership change or closure.
Completes admission evaluations, registry checks and family contacts; coordinates transfers and property return.
Carries out immediate transfers, notifies the administrator, representative and physician and documents the event.
Prepares refund calculations and issues refunds on time.
Receives notices and may use the complaint process and Ombudsman access.

documentation: Pre-admission screening and Admission Evaluation form
Physician evaluation on the DCH form
National Sex Offender Registry or fingerprint check result
Signed admission agreement with refund policy and discharge procedure
Written notice of discharge or transfer (30-day) or immediate transfer notice
Transfer or discharge summary with medication list
Property inventory and resident funds reconciliation
Refund calculation, check or transfer record and itemized statement
Notice to DCH of change of ownership or closure

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Training and Ongoing Evaluation (Including Memory Care and Proxy Caregivers)
policies.applies_to: PCH
policies.purpose: To make sure every [AGENCY NAME] staff member is qualified, trained before and during the work, and evaluated regularly, including the specialized training required when the home offers memory care or allows designated proxy caregivers.
policies.policy:
This policy meets PCH .07(3)(d) (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07(3)(d)) — training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SUPERVISION. On-site managers and responsible staff persons are at least 21 years old. No one under 18 works unless directly supervised in line of sight at all times (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.09).

TRAINING OF NEW STAFF. Each new staff member completes work-related training, including emergency first aid and CPR certification, within the first 60 days of employment (Rule 111-8-62-.09). CPR certification comes from a course that includes a hands-on skills demonstration.

MEMORY CARE TRAINING. If the home operates a memory care center, then under O.C.G.A. § 31-7-12.4 all staff receive at least 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation within their first 30 days. Direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of dementia training within the first 30 days of working independently with residents who have dementia, and at least 8 hours every year after. The home keeps documentation of course content, instructor qualifications, agendas and attendance rosters.

PROXY CAREGIVERS. Designated proxy caregivers are trained as Chapter 111-8-100 requires, and the home verifies that training before the proxy performs any task (PCH-12).

ONGOING EVALUATION. Each staff member's performance and competence are evaluated in writing at the end of the first 90 days and at least annually. Training records are kept for every staff member.

definitions.definition: The staff member in charge of the home and residents when the on-site manager is not present.
Staff who provide hands-on personal services to residents.
Training on the nature of dementia, communication, behaviors, person-centered care and safety, given to all staff in a memory care center.
Supervision by a qualified adult who can see the person at all times.
