Furnishings, linens and maintenance findings are reviewed each quarter in the quality assurance review (ALC-12 or PCH-11). The administrator documents corrective actions.
The administrator keeps maintenance requests, logs and completed repair records on site and available for DCH inspectors.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources, staffing and vendor contracts so furnishings, repairs and cleaning standards are met, and reviews the logs monthly.
Directs daily housekeeping, conducts the weekly safety walk, and corrects or escalates hazards immediately.
Clean, launder, inspect rooms, repair or report defects, and complete logs each shift.
Report hazards, help with linens and personal items, and keep resident rooms orderly and safe.

documentation: Room Readiness Checklist (per admission)
Housekeeping and laundry log (each shift)
Maintenance request and completion log
Weekly Safety Walk Log
Temperature log
Quarterly QA review notes

policies.category: Staffing and Personnel
policies.title: Background Checks, Registries and Fingerprint Determinations
policies.applies_to: ALC and PCH
policies.purpose: To make sure no owner, administrator, or employee with a disqualifying record has access to residents, and to keep registry checks and DCH reporting current.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes criminal background checks under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-12 as required by Rule 111-8-63-.09(11)-(13). Administrators and owners holding 10% or more of the community must complete a GCHEXS fingerprint check, and the determination letter must be dated within 12 months of the application. The administrator must have a satisfactory determination before serving. For certified medication aides (CMAs), the community checks the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry (111-8-63-.20). If an owner, director or employee acquires a criminal record, the community reports it to DCH within 24 hours (111-8-63-.30). This policy has no separate checklist items to tick off. It supports the DCH application requirements and the staffing and reporting rules.

definitions.definition: The Georgia Clearance for Healthcare Employees fingerprint check system used by DCH.
A written DCH or GCHEXS finding that the individual may work or serve under Ch. 111-8-12.
The Georgia registry that must be checked before a CMA is allowed to administer medications.

procedures: The administrator identifies every person who needs a check before hire: owners with 10% or more, the administrator, the on-site manager, all employees, and others as Ch. 111-8-12 requires.
Before any offer becomes final, HR or the administrator gives the candidate the fingerprint and consent instructions and the GCHEXS support contact: 404-463-7154, gchexs.user@dch.ga.gov.
The candidate completes fingerprinting. The administrator submits or confirms the request through GCHEXS and records the date submitted.

The administrator reviews the determination letter. The letter must be dated within 12 months for administrators and owners with 10% or more at application, and must be satisfactory before the administrator serves.

No person works in a role with resident contact until the determination required by Ch. 111-8-12 is in the personnel file. Until then, any permitted work is only under direct supervision as that chapter allows. The administrator records the basis.
If a determination is not satisfactory, the administrator does not allow the person to work or serve. The administrator consults the chapter's appeal procedure and records the outcome.

For each CMA, before assigning medication duties, the administrator or designee checks the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry and prints or records the result with the date and the checker's name.

The administrator repeats the registry check at each annual competency review and whenever a concern arises, and files the results with the competency documentation (see ALC-07 or PCH-06 and ALC-04 or PCH-03).
Each employee and owner must tell the administrator within one business day of any arrest, charge or conviction after hire. This duty is stated in the hiring paperwork and reviewed at orientation.

When the administrator learns that an owner, director or employee has acquired a criminal record, the administrator removes the person from resident contact pending review and reports to DCH within 24 hours, using the process in REC-02.

The report includes the community and administrator names, the date of the incident and the date of discovery, the incident type, a brief description, and the immediate corrective or preventive action.
The administrator records the check type, date, result and who reviewed it in the personnel file. Background check results are stored in a locked file and shared only with those who need them.
The administrator keeps a tracking log of all GCHEXS letters and CMA registry checks with dates, and reviews the log quarterly for missing or aging items.
Background check records are kept at least as long as the personnel file, which is 3 years after the employee leaves (STF-02).
Background check documents are kept ready for DCH inspectors, because inspections are unannounced and policies and records must be available for review.

Complete GCHEXS checks and keep the community informed of any change in their criminal history.
Verifies no one without clearance works unsupervised, and escalates concerns the same day.
Complete fingerprinting and report any arrest or conviction within one business day.

policies.category: Staffing and Personnel
policies.title: Hiring, Orientation, Employee Health and Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: ALC and PCH
policies.purpose: To hire qualified, healthy and properly oriented staff, and to keep the personnel records and staffing documents DCH requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires only staff who meet Georgia age, health, training and background requirements and keeps personnel files for 3 years after the employee leaves (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09(14)-(15); PCH counterpart 111-8-62-.09). The on-site manager and responsible staff persons are age 21 or older. No staff member under 18 provides care without line-of-sight supervision (111-8-63-.09(1)). Each employee has a TB screening and physical within 12 months before providing care (.09(10)). New staff complete orientation and required training within 60 days, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration for hands-on staff, and continuing education of 24 hours in year one and 16 hours each year after (.09(2)-(7)). Staff wear ID badges (.09(22)) and may not work impaired (.09(17)). Staffing plans and schedules are kept for 1 year (.09(21)). Administrators meet the qualifications under 111-8-62-.08 for personal care homes and hold the required Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license for assisted living. This policy has no separate checklist items to tick off.

definitions.definition: Employees who provide direct care or personal services to residents.
A trainee shows the instructor the skill (such as CPR) in person; reading or watching alone does not count.
Direct visual supervision of a staff member by an eligible adult staff person.

procedures: The administrator writes a job description for each position stating minimum age, duties, physical requirements and required credentials.

The administrator confirms qualifications before hire. The on-site manager and responsible staff must be 21 or older. Administrators must meet the qualifications for their program. For a PCH under 25 beds, that means age 21 or older and either an associate's degree or a GED or high school diploma plus 2 years of licensed PCH or healthcare experience. For 25 or more beds or assisted living, the administrator holds a valid Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license (Board: 404-424-9966), obtained within 60 days of hire where the rule allows that period.
HR collects a signed application and obtains the employment history, including prior employers and dates, and records any gaps or explanations in the file.
HR starts the background check under STF-01 before the employee has resident contact.

Before the employee provides care, the employee presents a TB screening result and a physical examination completed within the previous 12 months. HR files both and calendars the next due dates under the agency's health policy.

A candidate under 18 is hired only for a role permitted by Rule .09(1). Such a person always works within line-of-sight of an eligible adult, and the schedule shows who supervises. The 17-year-old exception applies only to a Georgia high-school nursing-assistant track student, and proof is filed.
The employee receives a photo ID badge on the first day and wears it at all times on duty.

On day one, the on-site manager gives orientation covering resident rights, abuse and neglect reporting, emergency procedures and evacuation, infection control, fire safety, confidentiality, and the policies in this manual. The employee signs an acknowledgment.

Within 60 days of hire, all staff complete the all-staff training and hands-on staff complete the hands-on training, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration. The trainer signs and dates a training record.
Staff who work in memory care or serve as proxy caregivers complete the additional training required by ALC-04 or PCH-03 and HLT-02 before assignment.
The administrator tracks continuing education hours for each employee: 24 hours in the first year and 16 hours each year thereafter. A tracking sheet is reviewed quarterly.

No employee may work impaired by alcohol or drugs. A supervisor who suspects impairment removes the employee from resident contact immediately, documents what was observed, and follows ALC-10 or PCH-09.
The administrator prepares written staffing plans and schedules and keeps them for 1 year, including the scheduled and actual hours worked (see ALC-02 and PCH-14).

HR keeps each personnel file with application, employment history, background check results, TB and physical, training records, competency checks, license or certification copies, signed acknowledgments and evaluations. Files are locked and confidential.
When an employee leaves, HR notes the separation date on the file and retains the file for 3 years from that date before authorized destruction.
Personnel files, training records and staffing plans are available to DCH inspectors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies qualifications, approves hires, ensures training deadlines are met and files are complete.
Conducts orientation, supervises staff under 18, and checks badges and impairment daily.
Collects employment history, TB and physical documents, and maintains personnel files and retention dates.
Provide accurate information, complete training on time and wear ID badges.

TB screening and physical records
Orientation checklist and acknowledgment
Training records and CE tracking sheet
ID badge issue log
Personnel file (kept 3 years after departure)
Staffing plans and schedules (kept 1 year)

policies.category: Records
policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: ALC and PCH
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, confidential file for every resident that is available to the people entitled to see it and to DCH.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps an individual file for each resident. The administrator or on-site manager is responsible for the file (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.24). Files are confidential and disclosed only to the resident, the resident's representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents, and anyone with written authorization. They are available for inspection and copying by the resident or representative and for inspection by DCH. Each file contains identifying information; the physician, hospital and pharmacy of choice; a record of monetary transactions with itemized receipts; a record and receipt of valuables held in safekeeping; health information (appraisals, diagnoses, diets, medications and orders); an inventory of personal valuables; the signed Resident's Rights form; the signed admission agreement; powers of attorney; any living will, durable power of attorney for health care or Georgia advance directive; and signed end-of-life medical orders. Records of accident, injury and death investigations are kept in the resident file and in a central quality assurance file (111-8-63-.26). Privacy practices follow 45 CFR 164.530 and RR-05. This policy has no separate checklist items to tick off.

definitions.definition: The single confidential record kept for each resident that holds the items listed in this policy.
A person with legal authority to make decisions or receive information for a resident, such as an agent under a power of attorney or advance directive.
A separate file where copies of investigations and incident follow-up are kept for quality assurance review.

procedures: At admission, the administrator or on-site manager opens a resident file and assigns it a file identifier.
The admission staff member records identifying information and the resident's choice of physician, hospital and pharmacy.
The signed Resident's Rights form and the signed admission agreement are placed in the file on or before the admission date.

Admission staff ask whether the resident has a power of attorney, living will, durable power of attorney for health care, Georgia advance directive or signed end-of-life medical orders, and file copies. If the resident has none, staff offer the Georgia forms at admission and note the resident's response (see RR-04).
The nurse or designated staff add health information as it is received: appraisals and assessments, diagnoses, diets, medication orders and physician orders (see ADM-02 and ALC-07 or PCH-06).

Any money handled for the resident is recorded as a transaction with an itemized receipt in the file. Valuables held in safekeeping get a written receipt and an entry in the file. An inventory of personal valuables is completed at admission and updated when items change (see RR-03).

After any accident, injury, change in condition or death, the on-site manager records the change and the response in the resident file the same shift, and notifies the representative or legal surrogate.

The administrator or on-site manager begins an immediate investigation of the cause of an accident, injury or death and reports to the representative or legal surrogate. Copies of the investigation go in both the resident file and the central QA file.
Files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the administrator, on-site manager and staff who need the information to care for the resident may access it.

Staff disclose information only to the resident, the representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents, or a person with the resident's written authorization. Each authorization is signed, dated and filed, and staff verify identity before releasing anything.

When the resident or representative asks to inspect or copy the file, the administrator or on-site manager arranges access within [NUMBER] business days and records the date and what was provided. No fee is charged beyond reasonable copying cost.
When DCH inspectors ask for files, the administrator or on-site manager provides them immediately and stays with the files while they are reviewed.
The administrator audits a sample of files every quarter for missing items, and adds the results to the QA review (ALC-12 or PCH-11). Missing items are fixed within 7 days.
At discharge or death, staff complete the file, record the date and circumstances, and move it to locked closed-file storage.

The governing body sets in writing, with legal counsel, a retention period for closed resident files, [RETENTION PERIOD]. The retrieved Georgia rule text confirmed no resident-file retention period, so the agency's period is documented as an agency decision. Records are not destroyed while an inspection, complaint, investigation, audit or legal claim is pending.

Documentation required by 45 CFR 164.530 (privacy policies, complaints, training and similar records) is retained in line with RR-05 and counsel's advice, and records are destroyed only by a method that protects confidentiality (shredding or secure electronic deletion).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures files are complete, confidential and accessible to authorized persons; sets retention with the governing body; leads investigations.
Maintains files day to day, records changes in condition and incidents, and grants inspection access.
Record observations and care accurately and promptly; protect resident information.
Provide documents such as advance directives and powers of attorney, and may inspect and copy the file.

documentation: Resident file index/checklist
Signed Resident's Rights form and admission agreement
Authorization-for-release forms
Money transaction records and receipts
Valuables receipts and personal inventory

policies.category: Records
policies.title: Required Reports to DCH
policies.applies_to: ALC and PCH
policies.purpose: To make sure every incident, Mattie's Call, inspection response and contact update is reported to DCH on time and with the required content.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reports to DCH within the deadlines in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.30. Within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing, staff call local police (Mattie's Call Act), and the community reports the start and the end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement. Within 24 hours of the incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred, the community reports to DCH: an accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness; a serious injury needing medical attention; rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation (Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act); an external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation; and an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record. The community disputes an inspection report in writing within 10 days of receipt if it chooses to, submits a written plan of correction within 10 days with date-certain actions, and displays the most recent inspection report and plan of correction where residents and visitors can see them (111-8-63-.10). The community keeps DCH supplied with current contact information and keeps its residential care profile accurate (111-8-62-.07 for PCHs; 111-8-63-.10). This policy has no separate checklist items to tick off. DCH may open a separate complaint investigation after any report.

definitions.definition: An event in the 24-hour reporting list: unanticipated or accidental death, serious injury needing medical attention, rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect, exploitation, external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation, or an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record.
The Georgia alert for a missing elderly or disabled person; police are called within 30 minutes of actual knowledge.
The community's written response to an inspection report listing each action to be taken and the date it will be completed.

procedures: Any staff member who sees or suspects a reportable event tells the on-site manager and the administrator immediately, and no later than the end of the shift.

For a missing resident, the first staff member with actual knowledge starts the search under SAF-01. The on-site manager calls local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge and records the time of knowledge and the time of the call.

When police are contacted for a missing resident, the administrator or on-site manager reports the start of the Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of that contact, and reports the end within 30 minutes of the contact that ends it. Times are logged.

For every other event on the 24-hour list, the administrator decides immediately whether it is reportable. If there is reasonable cause to believe a reportable event happened, it is reported. When in doubt, report.

The administrator submits the report to DCH within 24 hours of the incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred, using the method DCH designates for incident reports [DCH REPORTING METHOD].

Every report includes the community name and the administrator name; the date of the incident and the date of discovery; the incident type and a brief description; and the immediate corrective or preventive action.
The administrator also notifies the resident's representative or legal surrogate, and where abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected follows the mandatory reporting steps in ALC-09 or PCH-08.
When an owner, director or employee acquires a criminal record, the administrator reports it to DCH within 24 hours of learning of it (see STF-01).
The administrator saves a copy of each report and DCH's acknowledgment, if any, in the central QA file and, if a resident is involved, the resident file (REC-01).
If DCH opens a separate complaint investigation, the administrator cooperates fully, provides records on request and logs each contact.
When an inspection report arrives, the administrator records the date received, reads it with the governing body, and decides within 3 days whether any finding will be disputed.
Any dispute is submitted in writing to DCH within 10 days of receipt of the inspection report, with supporting documents.

The administrator submits a written plan of correction within 10 days of receipt, with a specific completion date for each corrective action and the person responsible. The administrator then tracks each action to completion and keeps proof.

The administrator posts the most recent inspection report and plan of correction where residents and visitors can see them. If the community has a website, the administrator adds a link to the previous 18 months of inspection reports and plans of correction and checks it each quarter.

The administrator confirms at least every quarter and after any change that DCH has current contact information for the governing body and the administrator or on-site manager (names, email for notices, physical addresses and phones), including the notice email (pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov is DCH's program contact), and that staff know to route DCH notices to the administrator the same day.

The administrator reviews the residential care licensed profile every quarter and after any change in services, beds or leadership, and corrects it with DCH. Marketing and services must match the license, profile and rules, and the administrator reviews marketing materials before release (GOV-01).
The administrator keeps a Report Log of all reports to DCH with dates, times, type, who submitted and follow-up, and reviews it quarterly in the QA meeting.

responsibilities.duty: Makes all DCH reports within deadlines, submits disputes and plans of correction, and maintains contact information and the profile.
Calls police within 30 minutes for a missing resident, preserves facts, and alerts the administrator at once.
Ensures DCH has current contact information and that staff are accountable for delivering notices to it.
Report suspected incidents immediately and never delay or discourage a report.

policies.category: Medicaid Waiver Participation
policies.title: Medicaid Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE ALS), EVV and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: ALC and PCH (only where the community is enrolled and approved for Alternative Living Services)
policies.purpose: To participate in the Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program accurately, protect waiver residents' rights, and bill Medicaid only for services actually delivered and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] participates in the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CMS waiver 0112.R08.00, CCSP and SOURCE) only after provider enrollment is approved. Alternative Living Services (ALS) covers 24-hour supervision in licensed personal care homes. Waivers do not pay room and board. Secondary sources give a resident room-and-board payment of $768 per month, leaving $226 of the $994 SSI benefit for personal needs, effective 1/1/2026. The administrator confirms the current amount with the Georgia DHS Division of Aging Services before quoting it. The community enrolls through the Georgia Medicaid GAMMIS portal before billing, because retroactive enrollment is not permitted, and completes revalidation on time. Where electronic visit verification (EVV) applies, the community uses the state EVV system (Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+). Personal support services under CCSP and SOURCE are listed under HCPCS T1019, and applicable claims with dates of service on or after September 14, 2026 must go through EVV. Whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself is unverified, so the administrator confirms with DCH in writing. Waiver residents receive services in a setting that respects the rights, choices and person-centered plan requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c). This policy has no separate checklist items to tick off.

definitions.definition: Community Care Services Program, one of the two programs under the Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver.
Service Options Using Resources in a Community Environment, the other program under the Elderly and Disabled Waiver.
Alternative Living Services, the waiver service providing 24-hour supervision in a licensed personal care home.
Electronic visit verification, the system that records the time, place and type of certain Medicaid home and community-based service visits.
The Georgia Medicaid provider enrollment and claims portal.

procedures: The administrator decides with the governing body whether the community will serve waiver residents and records the decision in the minutes.

Before accepting any waiver resident, the administrator completes GAMMIS provider enrollment and keeps the approval notice. Billing begins only after the effective date of enrollment, because retroactive enrollment is not allowed.

The administrator calendars each revalidation deadline 90 days in advance and completes revalidation before it expires. The waiver is listed by CMS as expiring 11/08/2027, so the administrator also watches for DCH and CMS notices on renewal.

Referral and entry: applicants start with an Area Agency on Aging assessment and screening through the statewide line 866-552-4464 (866-55-AGING). DFCS determines Medicaid financial eligibility and keeps the waiting list. Admission staff tell families that the community does not control eligibility or placement on the waitlist.
Admission staff do not admit a waiver resident until the program's approval or service authorization is in the file, and file a copy of the authorization (see ADM-01 and REC-01).

Staff explain in writing before admission that waivers do not pay room and board, and give the family the current room-and-board amount confirmed with DHS (secondary sources: $768 per month, effective 1/1/2026, leaving $226 for personal needs). The charge appears in the admission agreement (RR-02) and is never raised above the program amount for waiver residents.

The administrator never charges a waiver resident or family for a service that the waiver pays, and never requires a deposit or extra fee not allowed by the program. Any question is referred to DCH or the care coordinator in writing before a charge is made.
The personal needs allowance is protected. The community manages resident money only with written authorization and follows RR-03.

Services are delivered in line with the resident's person-centered service plan and the assessment (ADM-02). The administrator maintains a setting that honors choice, privacy, dignity, visitors and rights (ALC-06 or PCH-05).

The administrator confirms with DCH in writing, and files the response, whether EVV applies to the ALS service and to any personal support services (HCPCS T1019) the community delivers. Until confirmed, the community plans to be EVV-ready for dates of service on or after September 14, 2026.
Where EVV applies, the administrator obtains Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+ access, trains each caregiver before first use, and assigns each worker a unique login.

Caregivers record each visit in EVV at the time of service, at the resident's location. The on-site manager reviews the EVV exceptions report at least weekly and corrects missed or manual entries with a documented reason.

Before submitting any claim, the billing designee matches the claim to the service authorization, the EVV record where required, the daily service notes and the schedule, and bills only for services actually delivered and documented.

If an error is found in a submitted claim, the administrator corrects or voids it promptly through the proper channel and records the cause and fix. Overpayments are reported and returned. No staff member may alter records after the fact to support a claim.
Staff who suspect fraud, waste or improper billing report it to the administrator without fear of retaliation. The administrator investigates, corrects and documents.

The administrator reviews a sample of waiver claims against records every quarter as part of QA (ALC-12 or PCH-11), and keeps billing, EVV and service records for audits for the period required by Medicaid and the governing body's retention policy [RETENTION PERIOD].

responsibilities.duty: Maintains enrollment and revalidation, confirms rates and EVV scope with DHS and DCH, and certifies billing accuracy.
Reconciles authorizations, EVV records and service notes before each claim, and keeps audit files.
Ensures services and EVV entries are completed as planned and reviews exceptions weekly.
Deliver and document services accurately and use EVV correctly where required.
Approves waiver participation and receives quarterly compliance reports.

official.notes: No single DCH policy-review form exists for Georgia ALCs or PCHs, so the rule sections above are used instead. The rule lists the topics only as lettered paragraphs with no headings, so use the lettered items as the manual's categories. Section names are not invented. Use the ALC list for 25+ beds (Ch. 111-8-63) and the PCH list for 2–24 beds (Ch. 111-8-62). The two lists differ in order and wording: the ALC list adds the certified medication aide reference in (h) and orders its staffing-ratio item as (b), while the PCH list puts the staffing plan last as (p). Both rules say the lists are a 'minimum', so they are not exhaustive.
